sections.heading: 2. Make market comparisons and upstream economics survive contact with reality
paragraphs: The fourth trap is selling apparent cross-venue arbitrage between contracts that do not settle identically. A Kalshi event contract, a ForecastEx contract available through an authorized channel, and a sportsbook proposition can disagree on settlement source, deadline, cancellation, overtime, or exceptional events. An apparent four-cent probability gap is meaningless when one contract counts overtime and another excludes it. Normalize event identifiers, outcome wording, settlement authority, fees, depth, and executable size before presenting a comparison. An illustrative $1 contract bought for $0.48 against an independently estimated 0.51 probability has three cents of modeled gross edge; two cents of transaction cost and one cent of slippage remove it completely. Estimation error can make the result worse. Sportsbook decimal odds of 2.10 imply about 47.62% before adjusting for the full market's overround; that is not automatically comparable to a contract's displayed midpoint. Label the observation time and calculation method. Suppress positive-EV labels when matching is incomplete or available depth cannot support the displayed size. The safe fallback is an informational comparison with explicit differences, not an asserted executable hedge or a promised return.

The fifth trap is mistaking a fast WebSocket connection for a reliable market feed. Transport latency, upstream publication age, sequence gaps, and local processing delay are different measurements. For an illustrative liquid-market service target, flag quote age above one second and suppress actionable comparisons above two seconds; tune both limits to documented venue cadence rather than presenting them as universal rules. A quiet market requires heartbeat evidence, not fabricated price updates. Record monotonic receive time, source timestamps where supplied, sequence identifiers, and snapshot version. On reconnect, rebuild state from the provider's supported snapshot and replay procedure; do not stitch an old order book to new deltas blindly. Separate a genuine empty book from a missing update. The sixth trap is treating accessible feeds as commercially redistributable. Obtain rights for storage, derived displays, attribution, and downstream use from each provider; a public endpoint alone supplies none of those permissions. Use token buckets, bounded retries, and provider-specific budgets. A rate-limit response must reduce traffic rather than trigger account rotation. If authorized live access fails, show clearly timestamped historical analytics or disable the affected instrument instead of silently substituting scraped sportsbook prices.

The seventh trap sits inside free_tier_api_waterfall_multiplexing: free requests are not free resale rights. Its specified design aggregates 30–60+ B2B data, email-verification, firmographic, DNS, and SERP providers offering roughly 50–1,000 monthly developer lookups each. Forty providers averaging 250 permitted lookups yield 10,000 raw monthly calls, not 10,000 complete enriched records. At two calls per cache miss and an 80% fresh-cache hit rate, 20,000 requested records consume 8,000 calls, leaving 2,000 for retries and exceptional fields. Ten customers at $199 monthly produce $1,990 subscription billings; $150 hosting and $400 support leave $1,440 before acquisition, other labor, and overhead. This is a standalone sensitivity example, not additional scorecard revenue. Maintain 40+ interchangeable adapters, Postgres field provenance, expiry rules, and contractual resale flags. Prioritize the local graph cache when quotas tighten, then use permitted direct public-web, DNS, and MX extraction for business records only. MX existence does not prove mailbox deliverability. Exclude providers prohibiting aggregation or resale, honor shared account quotas, and degrade record completeness visibly. Never multiply free accounts, evade blocks, or enrich individual bettors with unrelated personal attributes to rescue unit economics.

callout.title: Veteran tactics for preserving evidence and negotiating leverage
callout.body: The best protection is a reproducible record that survives a provider change, operator dispute, or apparently profitable anomaly.
items: Keep a settlement-difference registry for recurring event pairs; one cancellation-rule mismatch should suppress every affected comparison automatically.
Replay recorded authorized feed sequences through the exact production normalization version before enabling a revised probability alert.
Negotiate deduction definitions, invoice-level reason codes, dispute deadlines, and negative-carryover scope before negotiating a higher headline RevShare.
Store provider permission versions beside waterfall adapter versions so quota savings never conceal a changed resale or retention restriction.

sections.heading: 3. Reconcile qualified deposits to collectible commissions, not dashboard celebrations
paragraphs: The eighth trap is optimizing to raw first-time-depositor events instead of contract-qualified, collectible CPA. An illustrative campaign buys 120 candidate depositors at $180 acquisition cost each, or $21,600. At $300 headline CPA, gross expected commission is $36,000. A 15% invalidation rate removes $5,400, leaving $30,600 before $3,000 servicing costs and $21,600 acquisition costs: only $6,000 contribution. The effective commission per candidate is $255, not $300. Duplicate accounts, existing customers, excluded locations, chargebacks, minimum-deposit failures, and prohibited traffic sources can all defeat qualification, but only the actual contract determines the applicable reasons and timing. Record click, registration, deposit, qualification, reversal, invoice, and cash dates as separate states. Use operator-supported signed S2S callbacks, idempotent event keys, and server-held secrets; never let browser parameters declare an earned commission. Compare mature cohorts rather than yesterday's incomplete traffic. Investigate a five-percentage-point increase in reversals against the mature baseline, and pause a placement if expected contribution per candidate becomes nonpositive. These are initial business triggers, not regulatory limits. Keep reversal reason codes and appeal evidence without retaining raw payment credentials or excess identity records.

The ninth trap is reading NGR as a universal accounting definition. It is a negotiated commission base whose deductions can include bonuses, taxes, payment charges, administration, jackpot contributions, and adjustments. Start with an illustrative $50,000 gaming gross revenue figure, already distinct from stakes and deposits. Subtract $10,000 bonuses, $5,000 administration, and $5,000 taxes where the agreement permits those deductions: eligible NGR becomes $30,000. A 25% share produces $7,500 before carryover. If the contract carries an $8,000 negative balance at the commission-share level, current cash commission is zero and $500 remains negative. A balance carried at the underlying NGR level would produce a different result; store its level explicitly. This is the tenth trap: assuming each month resets or that losses cannot cross brands, countries, or players. Negotiate ring-fenced balances and a clear expiry or reset where commercially available. Never subtract the same bonus once inside NGR and again from the affiliate invoice. Alert when total deductions rise more than five percentage points against the mature contractual baseline, then reconcile each line before buying further traffic into that cohort.

Keep the Formula v2.0 scorecard intact while exposing its economic plumbing. Conservative revenue of $75,000 less $55,500 expenses equals $19,500 owner profit, or 26%. Base revenue of $362,500 less $224,750 expenses equals $137,750, or 38.0%. Scaled revenue of $650,000 less $325,000 expenses equals $325,000, or 50%. An illustrative Base allocation is $180,000 subscriptions, $12,500 permitted builder rebates, and $170,000 affiliate commissions after deductions. The affiliate bridge starts at $240,000 provisional commissions and subtracts $40,000 contractual bonus and administration deductions, $18,000 invalidations, and $12,000 share-level carryover absorption. Its $170,000 revenue less $72,000 CAC and $28,000 other affiliate costs contributes $70,000. Subscription and rebate revenue of $192,500 less $124,750 remaining expenses contributes $67,750, reconciling exactly to Base owner profit. These allocations illustrate the supplied totals rather than replace them. Assess principal-versus-agent presentation and variable consideration under ASC 606; neither deposits nor user trading volume become operator revenue. No separate retained_share factor was supplied, so do not invent one or apply another haircut to already net commissions. A cash reserve changes liquidity, not profit again unless a separate expense is actually warranted.

sop_steps.title: Freeze the cohort evidence
sop_steps.action: Export authorized event states, contract version, creative identifier, jurisdiction, and operator statement for the same mature cohort.
sop_steps.detail: Preserve event timestamps and stable pseudonymous identifiers; separate reporting delay from actual qualification failure.

sop_steps.title: Rebuild qualification and deduction bridges
sop_steps.action: Match every provisional CPA and NGR line to qualification, reversal, permitted deduction, and carryover records.
sop_steps.detail: Deduplicate callbacks and identify whether each negative balance exists at underlying NGR or commission-share level.

sop_steps.action: Reconcile earned commission, estimated reversals, invoiced amount, payment timing, and actual bank receipt independently.
sop_steps.detail: Record unresolved differences with owners and contractual dispute deadlines; do not convert delayed cash automatically into a second expense.

sop_steps.action: Calculate cohort contribution after CAC, servicing, contractual deductions, and expected valid reversals before restoring acquisition.
sop_steps.detail: Resume only the supported placement and jurisdiction; preserve the unaffected subscription service throughout the investigation.

sections.heading: 4. Cut spend before seasonality, concentration, and bans turn a leak into insolvency
paragraphs: The eleventh trap is annualizing NFL-season CPA rates into a twelve-month forecast. Repeat the earlier campaign after budgets tighten: 80 candidate depositors at $220 headline CPA yield $17,600 provisional commission. The same 15% invalidation rate leaves $14,960. Acquisition at $180 per candidate costs $14,400, and $3,000 servicing produces a $2,440 contribution loss. More volume accelerates that loss unless acquisition economics or fixed servicing change. Maintain sport-calendar cohorts, operator budget confirmations, and campaign-level stop dates. Track collectible commission per candidate against fully allocated acquisition and servicing cost, not a blended dashboard return inflated by older profitable cohorts. As an initial policy, stop a placement when its mature expected contribution is nonpositive; investigate sooner when commission per candidate falls 15% against its matched seasonal baseline. Never describe this stress case as a revised canonical forecast. It is a sensitivity test around the supplied Base case. The fallback is to reduce paid affiliate acquisition, retain useful subscription analytics, and renegotiate placement terms. Email reactivation also needs audience permission and suppression handling; repeated messaging to excluded or vulnerable users is not a substitute for a broken CPA spread.

The twelfth trap is using shortcuts that destroy the underlying distribution account. Fake depositors, self-referral rings, purchased identities, prohibited brand bidding, cloaked landing pages, fabricated testimonials, and unapproved incentivized traffic can trigger commission reversal, termination, and wider liability. Do not experiment with them to discover an operator's tolerance. Store approved traffic sources and creative versions, then reject campaign launches that do not match. Monitor unusual repeated device or payment-linked signals only through operator-authorized, privacy-conscious reporting; shared household patterns alone do not prove fraud. A suspected attribution defect calls for reconciliation, not accusations or concealment. Platform dependency is another asymmetric exposure: a single search account, payment processor, feed license, or affiliate operator can interrupt collections while payroll continues. Treat more than 35% of trailing ninety-day collectible revenue from one commercial counterparty as a concentration alert, not an automatic legal threshold. Maintain exportable customer entitlements, documented recovery procedures, and alternative authorized providers. An alternate account must never be used to evade a suspension. Preserve subscription access where permitted, remove the disputed dependency, and use the provider's documented appeal channel with a complete evidence package.

Build a daily exception sheet that connects product health to cash survival. Include quote suppression minutes, callback signature failures, unmatched qualified events, mature reversal percentage, deduction ratio, negative balances, receivable aging, and available cash after committed obligations. For an illustrative policy, investigate unmatched events above 1% after the contracted reporting window, quarantine every invalidly signed callback, and escalate invoices fifteen days beyond their contractual due date. Compare unrestricted cash with the next ninety days of payroll, hosting, acquisition commitments, and plausible contractual repayment exposure. The published $1,500–$10,000 monthly opex range is a planning input, not permission to omit CAC or contractor costs from the canonical expense bridge. Stress the largest counterparty's delayed payment and one season of reduced CPA together. If that combined stress consumes the operating buffer, stop discretionary acquisition before cutting monitoring or reconciliation. During an incident, preserve signed event evidence, revoke compromised credentials, disable only the affected surface, and notify contractual counterparts as required. Restore service after replay tests and cash-ledger reconciliation demonstrate that the original defect is closed. A profitable screen is insufficient evidence; collectibility and recoverability are the operating standard.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #49, ranked #18 of 49 with a 91/100 Money-to-Manpower Score, wins by selling useful analytics and measurable acquisition infrastructure, not by confusing customer wagering with operator revenue. This chapter maps 12 operator plays into a sourcing system: verified public signals, jurisdiction-aware qualification, paid technical pilots, and reconciled affiliate contracts. Start with one permitted event-contract analytics segment and one licensed gaming jurisdiction. Use a 300-account prospect cohort to target six signed wins over 2–6 months, then require observed economics before expanding. Canonical annual owner profits remain $19,500 Conservative, $137,750 Base, and $325,000 Scaled. Startup credits can reduce eligible infrastructure expense, but customer cash, permissioned data, and collectible net commissions determine whether the business works.

sections.heading: 1. Mine observable buying friction instead of broad gambling interest
paragraphs: Start with two separate prospect ledgers: organizations purchasing non-custodial analytics, and licensed operators purchasing attributable customer acquisition. For analytics, inspect public Kalshi documentation, ForecastEx access arrangements through authorized intermediaries, published market schedules, permitted developer communities, and job advertisements seeking market-data engineers. A release that changes an API field, a documented disconnect problem, or a research team manually matching contracts is stronger intent than a large social following. For gaming, use NJ DGE, PA PGCB, and MI MGCB operator and supplier records to establish identity and licensing status before studying public affiliate-program terms. Add operator earnings presentations, state revenue reports, affiliate-manager hiring, and dated promotion changes as business signals, not evidence that a particular budget exists. Record source URL, observation date, jurisdiction, suspected problem, reachable business contact, and the exact evidence supporting outreach. Review twenty new records each weekday and reject records without a concrete operational problem. Use SQLite for the evidence ledger and a small CRM for contact history; neither requires expensive enrichment subscriptions. Preserve only necessary business contact information. Do not harvest bettor identities, private community messages, self-exclusion lists, or account-level transaction histories to manufacture an audience. Public availability does not override platform access terms or redistribution rights.

Translate each signal into a testable offer before finding an email address. A terminal buyer with intermittent feeds receives a timestamped reliability diagnostic and a proposed paid dashboard pilot; an affiliate manager receives a state-specific comparison-page sample and an attribution test plan. Separate market probability, executable price, fees, spread, settlement definitions, and observation time in every sample. Two contracts with similar titles may resolve differently, so a cross-venue price gap is not automatically an executable edge. Use WebSocket subscriptions only where supported and contractually permitted; otherwise use approved polling or licensed feeds. Promise a measured service level after testing rather than describing every source as sub-second. Mine Google Search Console queries on owned pages for recurring workflow questions, then publish instrumented answers with a business-demo invitation. Prioritize queries about reconciliation, contract matching, latency, and jurisdiction coverage over generic betting tips. A page receiving 200 qualified visits and six demo requests has a 3% visitor-to-demo rate; it has not generated six customers. Record subscriptions, permitted builder payments, and licensed gaming commissions in different CRM opportunity types. This prevents a promising analytics pilot from silently becoming compensated transaction solicitation without the necessary registration analysis and contractual permissions.

The twelve-play matrix below is this chapter's operating map, not a claim that twelve separate upstream identifiers were supplied. Its named credit play, cloud_ai_startup_credit_aggregation_arbitrage, supports the other eleven through lower eligible infrastructure cash expense. Form a Delaware or Wyoming entity only for a genuine standalone product with its own records, ownership disclosures, and business purpose. Check current AWS Activate, Azure Founders Hub, Google Cloud for Startups, Cloudflare, OpenAI, and Anthropic program availability, eligibility, partner verification, expiration, and permitted use directly; published headline amounts and eligibility change. A hypothetical $25,000 award against $1,000 of eligible monthly usage offsets only $12,000 during a twelve-month validity period. It does not create $25,000 of sales or authorize combining incompatible awards. The play's advertised $50,000–$350,000 aggregate range is a research target, not a budget assumption. Apply through verified founder or incubator channels and retain written award terms. Never create shell startups to repeat introductory offers, resell API credentials, or assume credits transfer between entities. Maintain an exportable extraction pipeline and test a licensed open-weight Llama or DeepSeek model through vLLM where hardware supports it. A rehearsed failover reduces interruption risk; it cannot establish zero downtime without measured capacity and recovery tests.

sections.heading: 2. Qualify permission, buyer intent, and collectible unit economics
paragraphs: Build qualification around five scored dimensions worth twenty points each: lawful service scope, evidenced operational pain, reachable purchasing authority, technical readiness, and collectible contribution. Require eighty points and a named budget owner for a paid pilot; require complete permission evidence regardless of total score. Analytics publishing is not automatically outside CFTC registration merely because software never touches money. The commodity trading advisor definition and exclusions in 7 U.S.C. § 1a(12), registration requirements in 7 U.S.C. § 6m, and applicable exemptions in 17 CFR § 4.14 must be evaluated against the actual service. Compensated solicitation or order handling can raise introducing-broker questions under 7 U.S.C. § 1a(31) and 17 CFR § 1.3; accepting customer funds raises additional FCM issues. Document whether outputs are impersonal, whether compensation depends on transactions, and whether links, onboarding, recommendations, or routing change the activity. Do not hold funds, pool capital, collect trading credentials, or direct United States users to unlicensed offshore, crypto, or unlawful sweepstakes venues. If the classification remains unresolved, restrict the offer to the reviewed reporting scope and defer the disputed compensation feature. A customer signature does not establish regulatory permission.

For gaming prospects, verify the operator's exact contracting entity, permitted products, jurisdictions, supplier requirements, and permitted marketing channels. New Jersey casino-service requirements under N.J.S.A. 5:12-92 warrant specific review; Pennsylvania and Michigan classifications require their own regulator checks rather than borrowing a New Jersey determination. West Virginia and Ontario are separate expansion workstreams with local rules, not extra boxes on a United States campaign. This project uses a 21+ audience restriction; Ontario's legal gambling age is nineteen, so twenty-one is a stricter product choice there. Pair age screening with jurisdiction-aware presentation, accurate responsible-gaming resources, and operator-side eligibility verification. A website geolocation estimate cannot replace an operator's regulated location checks. Ask how self-exclusion suppression and prohibited targeting are handled without obtaining protected lists yourself. FTC endorsement requirements under 16 CFR § 255.5 make material affiliate relationships relevant to the comparison page itself, not merely an obscure footer. Use an obvious compensation disclosure beside ranked offers and keep paid placement distinct from measured product attributes. Archive dated operator authorization, regulator status evidence, creative versions, and allowed-channel terms. Recheck these records before launching a new jurisdiction or changing the acquisition method.

Underwrite each prospect with an acceptance-adjusted worksheet, not the advertised commission. An illustrative sportsbook cohort produces twenty accepted first-time depositors at $150 CPA, or $3,000 of operator revenue. Deduct $1,400 traffic acquisition, $300 content expense, $200 attribution expense, and a $150 contract-supported reversal allowance to leave $950 contribution before shared overhead. If only fifteen depositors qualify, revenue falls to $2,250 and the same expenses leave $200. Confirm whether duplicate customers, jurisdiction mismatches, delayed identity checks, or deposit thresholds cause rejection. For revenue sharing, define the contractual NGR starting point before subtracting anything. If $20,000 excludes neither bonuses nor administration, $3,000 bonuses and $1,000 administration leave a $16,000 commission base; twenty-five percent pays $4,000. If those expenses already reduce reported NGR, subtracting them again understates revenue. A prior $5,000 negative balance applied before the split reduces this example to $2,750; a different carryover convention produces different results. Obtain the actual formula and a worked invoice. Model half the acquisition volume during a budget contraction and a full settlement-cycle payment delay. Reject contracts whose deductions, carryover grouping, caps, or dispute rights cannot be expressed as reproducible arithmetic.

sections.heading: 3. Run a permission-aware cadence that sells a bounded first outcome
paragraphs: Use a six-month prospect cohort with explicit stage definitions. Start with 300 raw business records, retain 120 evidence-qualified accounts, reach forty-eight live conversations, complete twenty-four discovery sessions, issue twelve scoped proposals, and sign six paid agreements. Those transitions are 40%, 40%, 50%, 50%, and 50%; the complete raw-record-to-signature rate is 2%. These are planning assumptions, not observed industry benchmarks. A plausible six-win mix is three analytics subscriptions, two licensed affiliate agreements, and one publisher integration. An affiliate signature counts as a commercial win but contributes no commission until qualifying activity occurs under the contract. Track cash collection as a separate stage. During month one, finish entity records, scope review, source permissions, and the first sixty qualified accounts. Months two and three should produce initial discovery and bounded paid pilots; months four through six emphasize referenceable delivery and repeatable conversion. Three wins at the same assumed conversion rate require 150 raw records; ten require 500. Capacity and segment quality may change those rates, so expand only after measuring a completed cohort. When conversion misses, identify the failing transition rather than declaring that the entire market lacks demand or purchasing a much larger contact list.

Run a five-touch business cadence across twenty-one days, stopping immediately after an objection to further contact. On day one, send a short individual email naming the observed workflow defect and offering one relevant artifact. On day four, use a professional-network message only when the contact's role clearly matches the problem. On day eight, send the artifact with an explanation of its limitations and one measurable pilot objective. On day fourteen, request a brief working session through the established business channel; avoid unsolicited automated telephone or text campaigns. On day twenty-one, close the sequence with a useful checklist and explain that further contact will stop unless requested. Apply CAN-SPAM requirements in 15 U.S.C. § 7704 to commercial email, including accurate identity, required address information, and functioning opt-out handling. Maintain suppression records rather than deleting objections and accidentally reimporting contacts. A concise opening is: 'Your public integration note describes stale contract timestamps. We built a permitted-data comparison showing where freshness diverges. Would a fifteen-minute review with your feed owner help determine whether a fixed-price monitoring pilot is useful?' Do not claim customer results, operator relationships, latency measurements, or registrations that the evidence ledger cannot substantiate.

Sell a narrow acceptance test rather than an ambitious platform replacement. For an analytics prospect, offer a $500 diagnostic followed by a thirty-day $1,000 team pilot, with separately defined feed permissions, supported contracts, refresh measurements, and support hours. These are illustrative offer prices, not additions to the canonical annual cases. A five-hour diagnostic at $50 per contractor hour leaves $250 before overhead; a pilot requiring twenty hours at that rate has consumed its entire fee before hosting. Limit scope or change price instead of hiding the labor. For an affiliate prospect, offer a synthetic click-to-postback demonstration and a small approved placement test after contractual permissions are complete. Specify accepted event definitions, deduplication keys, attribution windows, reversal handling, and the reconciliation owner. For publishers, define display rights and revenue-share treatment before installing a widget. End discovery by asking which single outcome would justify renewal and who can authorize it. Send a one-page scope within one business day, including deliverables, dependencies, acceptance criteria, price, and invoicing milestones. Never exchange a discount for a favorable endorsement; negotiate a smaller scope or longer commitment instead. Record refusal reasons verbatim and use the objection matrix to distinguish fixable uncertainty from a structurally bad deal.

sections.heading: 4. Turn first wins into collectible contribution and a repeatable pipeline
paragraphs: Instrument every first deal so delivery produces the next sourcing signal. For SaaS, record activation date, active seats, supported instruments, measured freshness, support time, renewal date, and collected subscription cash. Keep forecast revenue separate from invoices and receipts. For affiliate traffic, use an opaque click identifier, allowed campaign metadata, jurisdiction classification, and server-to-server event identifiers; do not place personal information in URLs. Authenticate postbacks, prevent replay, deduplicate events, and distinguish registration, deposit, accepted FTD, reversed FTD, and paid commission. A browser conversion is not proof of an accepted depositor. Reconcile weekly against operator exports and monthly against the settlement statement. Investigate differences by campaign and event age before blaming the entire tracking stack. Give the operator a compact exception file with identifiers and timestamps, not an unnecessary customer dossier. When a pilot meets its acceptance criteria, ask for an introduction to one peer with the same workflow problem. Obtain permission before naming the customer or publishing results. Turn recurring support questions into owned documentation and search pages, then measure whether those pages produce qualified business requests. This closes the loop between delivered utility, inbound demand, and lower acquisition expense without relying on unsupported performance claims.

Manage acquisition spending against settled economics and seasonal capacity. After football season, an operator may lower CPA caps while search and content expenses remain unchanged. Confirm current caps before each paid campaign and maintain a subscription offer that solves a year-round research problem. Do not present casino acquisition as an automatic replacement; product permissions, audience suitability, and commission rules differ. If an affiliate manager offers a larger percentage but refuses a deduction schedule, request a worked settlement and dispute procedure before discussing volume. If a SaaS buyer asks for automated trading, explain that the current product delivers reviewed analytics and keep execution outside the agreed scope until separately assessed. If a publisher requests raw data resale, provide only the licensed display format. Protect cash by limiting each unproven paid cohort to a predetermined loss budget, such as $500, and stopping when acceptance-adjusted contribution becomes negative. That budget is illustrative and must fit available working capital. A $1,400 traffic invoice due today against commissions payable next month creates a funding gap even when eventual contribution is positive. Maintain a settlement calendar, unresolved-deduction register, and cash runway view alongside the lead pipeline; signed contracts alone cannot fund delivery.

Reconcile the operating plan to Formula v2.0 without changing its annual scorecard. One illustrative Conservative mix is $48,000 SaaS, $3,000 permitted builder payments, $18,000 accepted CPA commissions, and $6,000 net NGR commissions: $75,000 operator revenue less $55,500 total costs produces $19,500 owner profit at 26%, with 1 FT + 2 C. Base uses $216,000, $12,500, $96,000, and $38,000 respectively: $362,500 revenue less $224,750 costs produces $137,750 at 38.0%, again with 1 FT + 2 C. Scaled uses $360,000, $20,000, $180,000, and $90,000: $650,000 revenue less $325,000 costs produces $325,000 at 50%, with 2 FT + 3 C. These channel allocations are planning decompositions, not additional canonical inputs or first-six-month forecasts. Costs must include acquisition, contractors, hosting, licensing work, servicing, and settlement losses without double-counting deductions already reflected in commission revenue. Assess principal-versus-agent presentation under ASC 606 for publisher arrangements; use retained operator consideration where net presentation applies, rather than gross partner billings or an invented retained_share multiplier. Credits never become sales. Customer trading volume, wagers, deposits, and loan principal never enter these revenue totals. Reforecast timing and channel mix when evidence changes while preserving the distinction between targets and observed results.

sections.heading: 1. Qualify the territory, contract, and revenue rail before publishing
paragraphs: Start each property with a signed operating manifest containing its legal entity, approved territories, partner identifiers, data entitlements, monetization method, and accountable owner. Separate the analytics subscription agreement from every sportsbook affiliate agreement; a common website does not merge their permissions. For Kalshi or ForecastEx coverage, document the actual authorized distributor, available endpoints, refresh limits, redistribution rights, and contract identifiers. Do not assume both venues expose interchangeable public WebSocket feeds. Normalize event settlement terms before comparing probabilities, because superficially similar contracts can settle on different sources or deadlines. An alert remains analytics: the subscriber decides whether to trade through their own authorized account. The operator never receives customer deposits, pools capital, stores trading credentials, or submits orders under this blueprint. Evaluate the actual activity against the introducing-broker and futures-commission-merchant definitions in 7 U.S.C. 1a, the registration provisions in 7 U.S.C. 6d, and the commodity-trading-adviser perimeter where recommendations become personalized. A publisher label cannot override those facts. Until scope is resolved, disable transaction-linked compensation and retain only separately reviewed, impersonal research subscriptions. Record that decision with the product version so later feature changes reopen the analysis.

Gaming intake uses a different manifest: destination operator license, relevant affiliate or supplier registration determination, state targeting rules, approved creative, permitted incentive wording, and responsible-gaming resources. Treat New Jersey DGE, Pennsylvania PGCB, Michigan MGCB, and West Virginia Lottery requirements as separate work queues rather than one national permission. Ontario is a separate country-level operating configuration with AGCO and iGaming Ontario requirements, not another American state. This blueprint uses a conservative 21-plus audience policy throughout; that product restriction does not describe every territory's statutory minimum. Before displaying a monetized destination, resolve the visitor's territory through an approved geolocation service, suppress uncertain results, and apply the partner's eligibility rules. The licensed operator still performs its own identity, age, exclusion, and wagering-location checks. Preserve a pseudonymous click identifier and creative version, never a copy of identity documents merely for attribution. Clearly disclose the affiliate relationship beside recommendations under 16 CFR 255.5. Reject offshore, unauthorized crypto, and unlawful sweepstakes destinations even when their advertised commissions exceed licensed offers. Maintain a tested link-removal procedure and show current responsible-gaming contacts appropriate to the visitor's territory, including 1-800-GAMBLER where applicable.

Map twelve operating plays without pretending that twelve catalog identifiers were supplied. The named catalog play is serverless_edge_free_tier_empire_hosting; the other eleven are chapter-local implementation labels enumerated in the matrix. Use Cloudflare Pages for permitted static bundles and Workers only where dynamic functions are necessary. Evaluate Vercel, Netlify, GitHub Pages, and Supabase against their current commercial-use restrictions and quotas rather than assuming every free allocation permits this business. A conditional hosting experiment is 100 approved properties times $0.00 hosting per month, with locally compiled HTML and JSON uploaded as artifacts. That calculation excludes domains, licensed feeds, monitoring, labor, and acquisition; it never establishes zero business costs. Stop at a small number of genuinely useful comparison tools until each has distinct content and eligible traffic. Do not multiply accounts or properties to bypass provider limits. If an allocation becomes unsuitable, consolidate the sites, disable expensive dynamic paths, or pay for an appropriate plan from the existing software budget. The operating edge is reusable evidence and predictable delivery, not indiscriminate page production. Assign one owner to every play and attach its unit denominator, stop condition, and recovery action to the manifest.

sections.heading: 2. Build a serialized evidence ledger before connecting partner callbacks
paragraphs: The six modules below form one small executable SQLite reference when copied in order into a Python file. They deliberately implement a narrow workflow: approved positive-value invoices, full settlement, paid operating expenses, and one currency per database. Initialize the database once before starting workers; each worker then opens its own connection on a local disk with reliable locking. Do not deploy this file on an object store or an unsuitable network filesystem. The single writer acquires BEGIN IMMEDIATE before reading mutable state, and every state change, journal entry, and idempotency result commits together. Concurrent replay therefore cannot double-recognize a case through these functions. A busy timeout fails the request without acknowledging success; the caller retries the same event identifier and identical payload. The unique partner/external identifier also stops a duplicate intake disguised with another event identifier. Authentication, authorization, signature validation, payload size limits, and secret storage belong in the adapter before these functions. Treat their absence from this compact reference as integration work, not as permission to expose a database operation directly to an unauthenticated browser or partner callback.

Intake scoring is an eligibility switch, not a speculative estimate of player value. The trusted adapter resolves rights, territory, registration scope, and operator eligibility from maintained evidence; user-supplied booleans cannot satisfy those checks. The immutable amount represents an approved commercial unit, such as a $200 accepted CPA, not the customer's deposit. Verification requires earned revenue evidence: delivered subscription service, an approved builder statement, an accepted first-time-depositor qualification, or a finalized NGR waterfall. The requested verification/escrow state machine is implemented as an evidence reserve only. Intake can become rejected or verified; verified can become released after a bank-backed match. No state holds customer funds, and released means the operator's invoice was collected. Prepaid annual subscriptions need deferred revenue and monthly service recognition, so they remain outside this monthly earned-service example. Similarly, refunds, partial payments, currency conversion, and later clawbacks require explicit compensating-entry extensions before those features are enabled. Never edit an earned amount to hide a dispute. Preserve the original record and add a separately authorized adjustment workflow with its own replay key, evidence, and balancing entries when extending the reference.

Every journal row specifies equal debit and credit cents, giving the reconciliation view a transparent bridge between revenue, expense, receivables, and cash change. Integer cents avoid binary floating-point drift; rounding occurs once when the contractual invoice is prepared. A settlement references a canonical bank receipt allocation, and its unique key prevents that allocation from funding two cases. For a bulk remittance, the adapter must first construct immutable allocation lines whose sum equals the bank receipt; this reference accepts only those prevalidated full-invoice lines. Store bank and partner evidence in restricted storage and retain references rather than sensitive raw payloads in the ledger. The supplied test exercises concurrent identical verification, altered replay rejection, settlement mismatch rollback, duplicate settlement suppression, and accounting totals. It is included as executable QA, not represented as having been run here. Before production, add process-crash recovery tests, duplicate receipt tests across separate cases, restoration drills, and authenticated adapter tests. All outward financial actions remain outside these modules: they record observed receipts and expenses rather than initiating transfers. That separation avoids pretending a database transaction can atomically commit an unrelated bank or partner API action.

rows: Module 1 establishes constrained tables, immutable journal entries, and reconciliation view

# Module 1: schema and connection factory.
import hashlib
import json
import sqlite3

SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events (
    event_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    digest TEXT NOT NULL,
    result TEXT NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS cases (
    case_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    partner TEXT NOT NULL,
    external_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    rail TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (rail IN ('saas','builder','cpa','ngr')),
    cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (cents > 0),
    state TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (
        state IN ('intake','verified','released','rejected')
    ),
    evidence TEXT NOT NULL,
    UNIQUE (partner, external_id)
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS journal (
    entry_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    event_id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES events(event_id),
    case_id TEXT REFERENCES cases(case_id),
    rail TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (rail IN ('saas','builder','cpa','ngr','shared')),
    debit TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (debit IN ('receivable','cash','expense')),
    credit TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (credit IN ('revenue','receivable','cash')),
    cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (cents > 0),
    receipt_key TEXT UNIQUE,
    CHECK (
        (debit='receivable' AND credit='revenue') OR
        (debit='cash' AND credit='receivable') OR
        (debit='expense' AND credit='cash')
    ),
    CHECK (debit <> 'cash' OR receipt_key IS NOT NULL)
);
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS journal_no_update
BEFORE UPDATE ON journal
BEGIN
    SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'Journal entries are immutable');
END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS journal_no_delete
BEFORE DELETE ON journal
BEGIN
    SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'Journal entries are immutable');
END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS case_amount_fixed
BEFORE UPDATE OF cents, rail, partner, external_id ON cases
BEGIN
    SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'Case economics are immutable');
END;
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS reconciliation AS
SELECT
    rail,
    SUM(CASE WHEN credit='revenue' THEN cents ELSE 0 END)
        AS revenue_cents,
    SUM(CASE WHEN debit='expense' THEN cents ELSE 0 END)
        AS expense_cents,
    SUM(CASE WHEN debit='receivable' THEN cents
             WHEN credit='receivable' THEN -cents ELSE 0 END)
        AS receivable_cents,
    SUM(CASE WHEN debit='cash' THEN cents
             WHEN credit='cash' THEN -cents ELSE 0 END)
        AS cash_change_cents
FROM journal
GROUP BY rail;
"""

def connect(path):
    connection = sqlite3.connect(
        str(path), timeout=30.0, isolation_level=None
    )
    connection.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
    connection.execute("PRAGMA synchronous=FULL")
    connection.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000")
    return connection

def initialize(path):
    connection = connect(path)
    try:
        connection.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
        connection.executescript(SCHEMA)
    finally:
        connection.close()
Initialize before workers; use local reliable storage and restrict direct database access
Module 2 serializes writes and binds event identifiers to immutable payload digests
All workflow writes use the same transaction envelope; failed attempts remain unacknowledged
Module 3 records trusted eligibility evidence and deterministic zero-or-100 intake scores
Server adapters resolve evidence; public forms cannot assert eligibility or approved amounts
Module 4 recognizes earned invoices through a non-monetary verification reserve
State checks and journal creation share one lock; no customer-money escrow exists
Module 5 matches full invoice allocations and records actual paid operating expenses
Canonical bank allocation identifiers remain stable across retries and alternative callback deliveries
Module 6 supplies concurrent replay checks and exact ledger reconciliation assertions

# Module 6: executable replay, contention, and reconciliation checks.
def self_test():
    from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
    from pathlib import Path
    from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

    with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
        path = Path(directory) / "ledger.sqlite"
        initialize(path)
        connection = connect(path)
        record = {
            "case_id": "cohort-01",
            "partner": "licensed-partner-01",
            "external_id": "accepted-ftd-01",
            "rail": "cpa",
            "cents": 20000,
            "evidence": "restricted-evidence/intake-01",
            "noncustodial": True,
            "rights_verified": True,
            "territory_verified": True,
            "age_21_verified": True,
            "vendor_verified": True,
            "operator_verified": True,
        }
        intake(connection, "partner-01/intake/01", record)
        intake(connection, "partner-01/intake/01", record)

        def worker(index):
            local = connect(path)
            try:
                return verify(
                    local, "partner-01/verify/01", "cohort-01",
                    "restricted-evidence/earned-01",
                )
            finally:
                local.close()

        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) as executor:
            results = list(executor.map(worker, range(16)))
        assert all(result == results[0] for result in results)
        assert connection.execute(
            "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM journal"
        ).fetchone()[0] == 1

        changed = dict(record, cents=30000)
        try:
            intake(connection, "partner-01/intake/01", changed)
        except ValueError:
            pass
        else:
            raise AssertionError("Altered replay was accepted")

        try:
            settle(connection, "partner-01/cash/bad", "cohort-01",
                   "bank-01/allocation-01", 19999)
        except ValueError:
            pass
        else:
            raise AssertionError("Amount mismatch was accepted")
        assert connection.execute(
            "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events WHERE event_id=?",
            ("partner-01/cash/bad",),
        ).fetchone()[0] == 0

        settle(connection, "partner-01/cash/01", "cohort-01",
               "bank-01/allocation-01", 20000)
        settle(connection, "partner-01/cash/01", "cohort-01",
               "bank-01/allocation-01", 20000)
        expense(connection, "operator/expense/01", "cpa",
                "bank-out-01", 5000, "restricted-evidence/invoice-01")
        assert report(connection) == [("cpa", 20000, 5000, 0, 15000)]
        assert connection.execute(
            "PRAGMA integrity_check"
        ).fetchone()[0] == "ok"
        assert connection.execute(
            "PRAGMA foreign_key_check"
        ).fetchall() == []
        connection.close()

sections.heading: 3. Price accepted units and close each revenue rail independently
paragraphs: The Base bridge below is an illustrative composition of the supplied $362,500 annual operator-revenue target, not a claim about current partner offers. Analytics contributes 300 active monthly subscriptions at $50, or $180,000 annually. Builder software contributes 250 contractually permitted annual eligible units at $100, or $25,000; monthly amounts are accounting allocations, not fractional customer counts. CPA contributes 60 submitted monthly qualifications less ten rejected qualifications, leaving 50 accepted units at $200 and $120,000 annually. NGR contributes $37,500 annually after the explicit deduction waterfall. These streams sum to $362,500 without including wagers, event-contract turnover, deposits, account balances, or any customer's principal. Use separate invoice series and ledger rail values so a strong subscription month cannot hide an affiliate shortfall. The scorecard's gross-revenue label refers to the operator's earned revenue, not gross gaming activity. Apply the ASC 606 principal-versus-agent assessment to the actual arrangements: affiliate revenue here is the contractual commission retained, and the NGR example already applies its 25% retained share. Do not multiply that recognized commission by the share again. Record SaaS subscription fees separately from transaction-linked builder compensation throughout.

For NGR, assume one monthly partner statement begins with $25,000 of contract-defined gaming revenue attributable to the eligible cohort. Deduct $5,000 administration charges, $5,000 bonus charges, and $2,500 brought-forward negative carryover, leaving $12,500 commissionable NGR. At a 25% share, operator revenue is $3,125. The $25,000 starting balance is neither the operator's revenue nor the customer's total wagering handle. Actual agreements vary on taxes, processing charges, jackpots, fraud, high-roller policies, and carryover across products; map each deduction to a named statement field before forecasting. Never assume a negative balance disappears at month-end. The CPA example loses ten of 60 submissions, a 16.67% rejection rate, before recognition. Its $6,000 monthly acquisition budget therefore costs $100 per submitted qualification and $120 per accepted qualification, leaving $80 per accepted CPA before shared affiliate operations. Use separate eligible cohorts for CPA and NGR unless a signed hybrid contract explicitly permits both. Without that distinction, a spreadsheet can count the same player twice while a partner pays only once. Keep rejection reason codes and evidence deadlines visible to the acquisition owner.

Allocate monthly operating costs of $8,000 to analytics, $1,000 to builder software, and approximately $9,729.17 to the combined affiliate operation. The affiliate amount comprises $6,000 acquisition and approximately $3,729.17 of content, attribution, registration maintenance, contractor work, and allocated operations. Against $13,125 affiliate revenue, contribution is approximately $3,395.83, or 25.87%, after the NGR deductions and the stated acquisition expense. Annual total costs are $224,750, leaving the canonical $137,750 owner profit and 38.0% margin. This run-rate cost envelope exceeds the supplied $1,500–$10,000 monthly opex range; treat that range as an initial fixed-overhead planning envelope, not the full Base operating-cost total. Do not silently discard acquisition or contractor spending to force agreement. Post-NFL seasonality is a separate stress: six months at 60 accepted CPAs and six at 40 produce the same 600 annual accepted units, while a flat 50-per-month walk merely smooths timing. If commissions fall 20% for three months without replacement, annual profit falls $6,000 to $131,750 at unchanged cost. Reduce uneconomic acquisition, diversify eligible partners, or rebuild the target explicitly.

sections.heading: 4. Walk three earned cohorts through scrubs, operating costs, and bank cash
paragraphs: Begin the walk with zero opening receivables and a fully provisioned monthly service cohort, not with a newly launched site acquiring 300 subscribers overnight. Each month contains 300 active subscription-month units, 60 submitted CPA qualifications, 50 accepted CPAs, and a separately attributed NGR statement. Subscriber counts represent active service units, not 900 distinct people over the quarter. Builder revenue uses the annual allocation established above. Subscriptions are earned and collected within the service month; all builder, CPA, and NGR amounts are finalized at month-end and collected in the next month. No chargebacks, additional bad debts, taxes, capital purchases, or owner distributions enter this operating bridge. All modeled operating costs are paid in the month incurred. Those assumptions isolate the difference between profit and collection timing while retaining the supplied Base economics. A real startup still faces the stated two-to-six-month first-deal interval and $8,000–$45,000 capital range. Treat the walk as a steady operating cohort entering a new ledger, not as evidence that launch revenue arrives immediately. Maintain a separate startup cash schedule for development, registration work, deposits paid to vendors, and the acquisition ramp.

Month 1 earns $30,208.33 but collects only $15,000 of subscription cash. After $18,729.17 operating costs, cash change is negative $3,729.17 while earned operating profit is positive $11,479.16. The difference is $15,208.33 of partner receivables. Month 2 collects its own $15,000 subscriptions plus Month 1 partner invoices of $15,208.33, creating $30,208.33 receipts and $11,479.16 cash generation after the same expense amount. Cumulative cash change becomes $7,749.99. Month 3 again collects $30,208.33 because the previous cohort's builder allocation was $2,083.33; its own earned revenue is $30,208.34 because the rounding penny belongs to the current cohort. Expenses of $18,729.16 produce $11,479.17 cash generation and $11,479.18 earned profit. Quarter-end cumulative cash change is $19,229.16, and uncollected Month 3 partner invoices total $15,208.34. Adding those receivables to cash generation gives exactly $34,437.50 quarterly operating profit. The scrubs already reduced CPA recognition, and NGR deductions already reduced commission revenue; neither should be subtracted again during cash reconciliation. The receipt schedule records collection lag, not a second revenue-recognition event.

Use the closing review to turn variances into specific actions. An accepted CPA missing from the next remittance becomes an aged invoice assigned to the partner manager, not a new lead. An NGR discrepancy becomes a statement-field dispute with the contract version and carryover opening balance attached. A subscriber decline becomes a retention and replacement task before paid acquisition is increased. The reference's largest modeled operating cash drawdown is $3,729.17, but that is not sufficient launch capitalization: one extra month of partner delay would deepen cumulative cash drawdown to $7,458.34 before startup expenditures. Maintain at least the modeled exposure plus a documented delay reserve and the actual setup budget. Annualize the earned quarter, not its initial cash receipts: $90,625 times four is $362,500 revenue, $56,187.50 times four is $224,750 costs, and $34,437.50 times four is $137,750 owner profit. Conservative and Scaled remain distinct scorecard cases rather than multipliers applied to traffic volume. Close the first 90 days by proving the ledger bridge, replay behavior, territory exclusions, partner collectability, and restoration procedure before adding properties or expanding the team.

sections.heading: 1. Establish the legal entity, product, territory, and permission graph
paragraphs: Start with a permission graph, not a list of attractive odds. Represent every destination as a legal entity, consumer brand, approved domain, product class, territory, registration category, effective date, and evidence URL. The CFTC designated contract market list establishes exchange status; NFA BASIC helps check registrant identities and disciplinary history. Neither establishes that your particular referral arrangement is permitted. Read the exchange agreement and compare actual conduct with the introducing broker and futures commission merchant definitions in 7 U.S.C. 1a and 17 CFR 1.3. Never accept customer funds, pool capital, collect brokerage credentials, or transmit orders through an analytics product without separately resolving the applicable registration framework. A paid publisher also needs a documented assessment of commodity trading adviser rules; a publication label alone does not settle the question. Assign one evidence owner and one backup for each destination. Capture the official page, retrieval time, effective date, and a SHA-256 digest. A dated screenshot supports a review trail but cannot replace the operative order or license record. Recheck before activating a destination and whenever an official notice changes its scope.

Build a separate state gaming graph because a CFTC exchange record says nothing about sportsbook affiliate permissions. Consult New Jersey DGE, Pennsylvania PGCB, Michigan MGCB, and West Virginia Lottery records for the operator, approved brand, and relevant supplier or vendor treatment. Determine your own registration obligations from the compensation arrangement and activities rather than assuming every publisher uses one category. For Ontario, reconcile AGCO registration with iGaming Ontario's operator directory; Ontario is a separate jurisdiction, not an extension of a United States license. This chapter adopts a 21+ affiliate publishing floor even where the local minimum differs, including Ontario's 19+ threshold. Apply destination eligibility before presenting outbound promotional links, and use jurisdiction-specific responsible-gaming resources. IP location is an imperfect publishing filter, not a replacement for the operator's regulated identity and location checks. Do not route United States readers to unlicensed offshore or crypto venues or unlawful sweepstakes casinos. If a register is inaccessible, preserve the last verified record for investigation, suppress affected acquisition links, and request current written evidence from the operator rather than treating silence as continued authorization. Record who restored the destination and why.

The first nine directory entries are public evidence sources, not promised machine interfaces. Their no-charge access does not include engineering labor, bulk redistribution rights, or a service-level commitment. Use an official download when offered; otherwise conduct a modest scheduled page check consistent with published access conditions. Daily retrieval is an internal target for registers, while live launch decisions require a fresh check of the relevant record. Store publication time separately from retrieval time because a newly fetched page can still contain an old decision. Use conditional requests where supported, one outstanding request per host, bounded retries, and a circuit breaker after repeated failures. Treat an empty parser result as an incident, not proof that every license disappeared. Route structural changes to a human evidence queue. An enrichment waterfall should move from official entity record to official approved domain, then executed partner agreement, then internal campaign identifier. Reject fuzzy brand matches that join unrelated subsidiaries. This sequence prevents a cheap directory shortcut from creating expensive misdirected traffic. The practical output is a versioned destination manifest that both the publishing system and attribution service can read without independently interpreting license scope.

sections.heading: 2. Acquire permissioned feeds and normalize contracts before measuring speed
paragraphs: Separate discovery, quotation, and settlement into different pipelines. Kalshi documents market-data interfaces, including WebSocket access, but current authentication, account tiers, subscription limits, and redistribution terms must be verified in its official documentation and agreement. ForecastEx access may come through Interactive Brokers or another authorized distribution arrangement; do not invent a public ForecastEx WebSocket endpoint or assume a brokerage account permits commercial display. A commercial sportsbook feed such as Sportradar or The Odds API can accelerate coverage, yet feed availability does not establish affiliate permission or execution availability. Store provider identifier, venue identifier, contract identifier, source event time, receipt time, sequence number when supplied, and rights classification on every normalized record. Design for at-least-once delivery and deduplicate by stable identifiers rather than arrival order. The next nine directory entries distinguish public documentation from paid entitlements and self-hosted software. Their stated refresh cadences are operating targets, not vendor promises. Obtain written quotes for commercial access instead of embedding transient list prices into the business model. Keep a cheaper read-only fallback, but never silently replace a licensed real-time stream with scraped consumer screens.

Cross-venue normalization is a contract interpretation problem before it is a probability calculation. Two election contracts can reference different certification authorities, deadlines, recount treatment, cancellation rules, or payout conditions. Sportsbook prices introduce overtime rules, pushes, voided legs, stake limits, and location-dependent availability. Attach a versioned settlement-rule fingerprint to each comparison pair and require an exact reviewed mapping before calling prices comparable. For an illustrative binary contract bought at $0.54 with an estimated $0.02 transaction cost, a research probability of 0.60 produces expected profit of $0.04 per contract before slippage and model error. That is analytics output, not operator revenue or an executable riskless spread. A sportsbook decimal price of 1.90 implies approximately 52.63% before removing the bookmaker margin; it does not directly equal a clean probability estimate. Show displayed size, applicable fee assumptions, rule differences, and source timestamps alongside every comparison. If either quote is stale or a rule mapping changes, suppress the positive-edge badge and retain a historical chart. This fallback protects subscriber trust without manufacturing certainty from mismatched contracts or unavailable liquidity.

Instrument the feed path before marketing sub-second alerts. Measure provider event time to receipt, receipt to normalization, and normalization to rendered alert separately; clock skew can otherwise make a slow system appear fast. An illustrative internal budget of 300 milliseconds for transport, 200 for normalization, and 300 for delivery totals 800 milliseconds only where the source genuinely supplies timely events. Polling every five seconds cannot support that claim. Apply token buckets per credential and endpoint, honor Retry-After, and reconnect with capped exponential backoff plus jitter. After a disconnect, recover from a documented snapshot and resume sequence only where the provider supports that method. Otherwise mark the interval incomplete and rebuild current state without claiming tick-perfect history. sections.heading: 3. Turn verified evidence into comparison content and measurable subscriber value
paragraphs: The chapter's twelve mapped plays connect evidence acquisition to revenue, with six infrastructure plays below and six commercial plays in the final matrix. The required competitor_intent_comparison_hijacking play belongs to TRACK_2: build useful pages for '[Competitor] pricing', '[Competitor] cancel', and '[Competitor] vs [Offer]' queries. Treat the name as an internal acquisition label, not permission to impersonate a competitor or interfere with cancellation. Publish text-only brand references, timestamped public pricing citations, honest feature matrices, and direct links to the competitor's own cancellation instructions. Nominative fair use is context-dependent; keep references necessary, accurate, and free of implied endorsement. Do not copy logos, fabricate affiliations, or describe a paid placement as an independent ranking. Disclose material affiliate relationships clearly near relevant recommendations under 16 CFR 255.5. If a fee cannot be verified, remove that calculation and show the source-check date instead. Programmatic publishing should require a complete evidence record for each claim, not merely a template and a keyword. A broken source should automatically retire affected factual claims while preserving genuinely useful explanatory material that remains supported.

Use the proposed 10–18% conversion range as a test hypothesis for qualified comparison visitors, not an assumed sitewide result. At 1,000 qualified visits, a 10% paid conversion produces 100 subscribers; 18% produces 180. At an illustrative $40 monthly subscription, those cohorts create $4,000 or $7,200 of first-month billed subscription value before refunds, payment costs, churn, and tax treatment. With $6 variable service cost per paid subscriber, first-month contribution before acquisition and shared overhead is $3,400 or $6,120. If traffic costs $2,500, the remaining amounts are $900 and $3,620. These cohort examples are not additional scorecard revenue and cannot be annualized without retention evidence. Measure completed paid starts separately from free account creation, then reconcile paid starts against processor settlements. Segment direct SaaS buyers from sportsbook affiliate referrals so one click does not receive two incompatible revenue assumptions. A cancellation guide can convert by solving an urgent user problem, but it must never obstruct the original cancellation. When paid traffic misses its contribution threshold, stop buying that segment and retain the evidence-backed organic page.

Design calculators around reproducible inputs rather than persuasive output. A fee calculator should expose contract quantity, quoted price, applicable fee schedule, subscription charge, and the timestamp of every external assumption. Retain a calculation version so support can reproduce what a reader saw. An enrichment waterfall for comparison content starts with the venue's official rulebook and pricing page, then a permissioned market feed, then an executed partner schedule, and finally an editor-confirmed exception. Do not enrich individual readers with purchased gambling propensity or vulnerability indicators. Use campaign-level attribution and the minimum identifiers required for reconciliation. For migration guides, accept only customer-authorized exports and document which watchlists or research settings can actually move; never request brokerage passwords. Subscription retention should be earned through reliable alerts, transparent methodology, and fast defect resolution. At 400 active subscribers, reducing monthly voluntary churn from 5% to 4% retains four additional subscribers for that month, worth $160 in billed value at $40 each before costs. That unit math supports a small reliability project, not an unlimited engineering budget. If retention does not improve, revert the experiment and examine cohort-specific failure reports.

sections.heading: 4. Reconcile attribution, deductions, and seasonality to the exact scorecard
paragraphs: Keep three ledgers: subscriptions, permitted builder arrangements, and licensed gaming affiliates. The first records your SaaS service revenue; the second records only contractually earned software or referral consideration after boundary review; the third records payable CPA and NGR commissions after contractual adjustments. Under an ASC 606 principal-versus-agent assessment, an affiliate generally reports its earned commission rather than customer deposits, sportsbook handle, or the operator's gaming revenue. Where retained_share applies to pass-through billings, multiply by that share once; never apply another haircut to a commission already reported net. An illustrative Base bridge is 400 average paid subscribers times $40 times twelve months, or $192,000, plus $20,500 of permitted builder consideration and $150,000 of net affiliate commissions, totaling $362,500. The affiliate component can comprise 1,000 finally approved CPA events at $120, yielding $120,000, plus $30,000 of NGR commissions from a separate eligible cohort. An NGR example starts with $200,000 gaming revenue, subtracts $50,000 contractual deductions, applies a 25% share to $150,000, and subtracts $7,500 carried losses from $37,500. The resulting $30,000 is operator affiliate revenue, not $200,000.

The Base scorecard allows $224,750 of total annual operating costs because $362,500 less $137,750 equals $224,750. An illustrative allocation is $60,000 acquisition, $74,000 staffed engineering and editorial work, $24,000 hosting and feeds, $21,750 verification and support, and $45,000 other operating costs, including remaining staff and administration. These amounts sum exactly to the allowed cost envelope; owner distributions are not an additional operating deduction. Deduct NGR bonuses and administration charges in the commission bridge, not again in overhead. The Conservative case remains $75,000 revenue less $55,500 costs, producing $19,500 at 26%. The Scaled case remains $650,000 less $325,000, producing $325,000 at 50%; Base remains 38.0%. Keep teams at 1 FT + 2 C for Conservative and Base, and 2 FT + 3 C for Scaled. Model sportsbook seasonality monthly without changing these annual totals silently. For example, four off-season months losing twenty payable FTDs each at $120 reduce expected CPA revenue by $9,600 unless other earned revenue replaces it. Treat that as a downside forecast variance, reduce marginal acquisition spend, and preserve the canonical scenario as the comparison baseline rather than pretending the gap disappeared.

S2S attribution needs a state machine, not a counter that increments whenever a callback arrives. Record click accepted, registration reported, first deposit reported, eligibility reviewed, commission approved, commission reversed, and cash collected as separate events. The operator determines the payable FTD under its contract, including age, territory, duplicate-account, minimum-deposit, and promotional conditions. Your publishing filter does not certify those conditions. Verify callback signatures, enforce timestamp windows, deduplicate partner event identifiers, and reconcile daily against exports. Reconcile monthly against settlement statements and bank receipts. Track negative carryover by partner and contractual cohort; do not spread it across unrelated partners to flatter performance. For a campaign costing $6,000 that produces eighty approved FTDs at $120, gross commission is $9,600 and contribution before shared costs is $3,600. Ten later reversals reduce those figures to $8,400 and $2,400. Maintain a reserve policy based on observed reversal timing and payment disputes. Pause spend when collected contribution falls below the acquisition threshold, when a partner reduces its CPA budget, or when evidence cannot support attribution. The final dashboard should explain every dollar from source event to collected cash.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #49, Regulated Prediction-Market Terminals & Licensed iGaming Affiliates, holds Rank #18 of 49 with a 91/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. Its 12 mapped plays combine non-custodial analytics, permitted referral software, licensed affiliate distribution, and evidence-backed settlement. The operating boundary matters more than the interface: publishing probabilities does not automatically exempt solicitation, personalized advice, or order activity from registration. Separate SaaS revenue from state-authorized CPA and NGR commissions, contract every deduction, and suppress prohibited destinations. Canonical annual owner profit is $19,500 Conservative, $137,750 Base, and $325,000 Scaled. This chapter turns federal definitions, jurisdiction-specific permissions, commercial clauses, hosted-publication placements, and verbatim outreach into a reproducible system that preserves attribution evidence without taking custody or confusing player activity with operator revenue.

sections.heading: 1. Classify every feature before selling access or referrals
paragraphs: Build two product lanes with separate contracts, ledgers, destination policies, and release records. Lane A sells non-custodial event-contract analytics and only those builder referrals expressly permitted by the relevant venue and applicable law. Lane B earns commissions from appropriately licensed sportsbook and casino operators where the affiliate has the required permissions. For this chapter, the 12 mapped implementation plays are subscription terminals, cross-venue probability comparisons, positive-EV alerts, historical research exports, permitted builder referrals, licensed CPA comparisons, NGR revenue sharing, geofenced attribution, owned-email education, permission-based SMS alerts, partner API distribution, and parasitic_seo. These are operating mappings, not assertions that every feature is authorized everywhere. Label each feature with its payer, user action, compensation basis, destination, and license dependency. A monthly research subscription differs materially from compensation tied to customer trading, even when both appear behind the same button. Never accept deposits, pool capital, take withdrawal credentials, or direct US users to unlicensed offshore or crypto venues or unlawful sweepstakes casinos. Maintain a feature inventory that distinguishes publishing, promotion, introductions, recommendations, and transaction handling. Assign an accountable owner to each classification and attach the evidence supporting its permitted scope before charging customers.

Apply the Commodity Exchange Act to conduct rather than marketing labels. Under 7 U.S.C. § 1a(12), compensated advice and analysis about covered commodity interests can implicate commodity trading adviser status; publisher exclusions and the regular-business conditions require a fact-specific examination. Registration obligations and exemptions also require analysis under 7 U.S.C. § 6m and 17 CFR § 4.14. Do not treat a general research label as permission to deliver individualized trade instructions. The introducing broker definition in 7 U.S.C. § 1a(31) matters because an IB can solicit or accept orders without accepting customer funds. Non-custody therefore does not resolve the registration question. The futures commission merchant definition in § 1a(28) addresses additional conduct involving customer money or property. Before adding account-linked alerts, referral compensation, prefilled tickets, or order connectivity, obtain a written classification covering the actual workflow and compensation. Verify Kalshi and ForecastEx permissions through current official venue documentation and agreements; a venue's regulated status does not authorize every intermediary activity. If classification remains unresolved, retain general research and remove the affected referral or transaction feature. Record the removed capability in the release manifest so engineering cannot silently restore it through a configuration change.

Translate market-data permissions into enforceable system behavior. A WebSocket connection does not itself grant rights to redistribute quotes, retain historical snapshots, train models, or sell derived feeds. Negotiate those uses separately for each source, including termination access and archival evidence needed for customer disputes. A sub-second engine should record exchange timestamps, local receipt timestamps, market status, and processing lag; it should not advertise executable cross-venue arbitrage when settlement definitions, fees, position limits, or available depth differ. Positive-EV labels need an explicit model version, price timestamp, fee assumption, and explanation that estimated probability can be wrong. Keep API secrets server-side and request the least privileged scope available; exclude trading and withdrawal authority from analytics integrations. Test a stale-feed fallback that disables actionable price comparisons while preserving historical research. For example, 120 subscriptions at $100 monthly produce $144,000 annual subscription revenue regardless of whether subscribers collectively trade $1 million or $100 million. If a builder arrangement separately pays $18,500 annually, recognize only the earned contractual software or referral amount after assessing its conditions. Neither user turnover nor hypothetical trading gains enter the publisher's revenue ledger. This separation also makes cancellation, access suspension, and revenue reconciliation independently testable.
