sections.heading: 2. Turn jurisdiction differences into executable distribution rules
paragraphs: Create a jurisdiction register at the product level, not merely the brand level. New Jersey internet gaming and sports wagering operate under distinct statutory provisions and Division of Gaming Enforcement rules; vendor classification depends on services and compensation, not the affiliate's preferred title. Review N.J.S.A. 5:12-92 and N.J.A.C. 13:69J for vendor obligations, together with the applicable internet gaming and sports wagering provisions. Pennsylvania combines the Pennsylvania Race Horse Development and Gaming Act with specific interactive gaming and sports wagering requirements; obtain the Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board's applicable supplier or vendor determination. Michigan separately regulates internet gaming under MCL 432.301 et seq. and internet sports betting under MCL 432.401 et seq.; record the Michigan Gaming Control Board classification for the services actually supplied. West Virginia requires its own product and supplier analysis rather than inheriting neighboring permissions. Ontario is a separate country and regulatory system involving AGCO standards and the operator's iGaming Ontario arrangements. Do not describe an Ontario registration as US authorization. For every destination, record the operator entity, product, credential requirement, permitted traffic source, approval evidence, renewal date, and responsible contact. Missing evidence suppresses monetized distribution rather than creating an assumed permission.

Use a 21-plus access policy across this volume's acquisition funnel, while accurately distinguishing that commercial choice from each jurisdiction's statutory age. Ontario generally uses 19 for regulated internet casino and sports betting participation; a stricter publisher policy does not change that rule. A birth-year screen and IP lookup are preliminary filters, not operator-grade identity verification or wagering geolocation. The licensed operator remains responsible for its required identity, exclusion, and location checks, while the affiliate must satisfy its own advertising and distribution duties. Configure server-side destination rules by jurisdiction, product, device signal quality, and campaign permission; fail closed when a monetized destination cannot be validated. Do not use VPN troubleshooting to help people bypass location restrictions. Present appropriate responsible-gaming resources and current local helpline disclosures next to commercial calls to action, not solely in a remote footer. Keep state-specific templates because required wording and resources can change. Block youth-oriented placements and audiences, prohibit claims of income replacement, and avoid messaging that encourages recovering losses. Preserve template versions and campaign screenshots so a later reviewer can reconstruct what the audience actually saw, including the destination and disclosure visible on mobile devices.

Separate federal truth-in-advertising requirements from channel-specific permission rules. Section 5 of the FTC Act, 15 U.S.C. § 45, prohibits deceptive commercial practices; 16 CFR Part 255 explains endorsement principles, including clear disclosure of material connections. Put an affiliate-compensation statement beside rankings and outbound links, and explain whether payment affects ordering. Quantified win-rate, return, speed, and ranking claims need evidence matching the stated population and period. Commercial email must satisfy CAN-SPAM, including accurate headers, a valid postal address, and an effective opt-out honored within ten business days. Do not assume that receiving a business card authorizes promotional texts. Automated calls and texts require a separate analysis under 47 U.S.C. § 227 and 47 CFR § 64.1200, including applicable permission, revocation, and do-not-call requirements. Ontario campaigns also require Canadian anti-spam and local marketing analysis; a US email process is not automatically portable. Collect only attribution fields needed to establish eligibility and payment, with defined retention and deletion rules. Send pseudonymous event identifiers rather than raw player identity documents. When rules conflict with a partner's growth request, narrow the audience or remove the channel instead of weakening evidence collection.

sections.heading: 3. Contract the fee waterfall and reconcile every profit case
paragraphs: Use separate schedules for software services and gaming acquisition. Define scope, territory, approved domains, eligible products, prohibited conduct, and change-control responsibilities. For CPA, define a first-time depositor with measurable requirements: new eligible account, verified identity, qualifying deposit, any lawful qualifying activity, attribution window, duplicate policy, and fraud exclusions. State whether payment depends on acceptance, settlement, or another specified event, and place a deadline on rejection with reason codes. For NGR, enumerate the starting measure and every permitted deduction rather than accepting an expandable administration category. Specify bonus treatment, gaming taxes, payment costs, chargebacks, negative carryover, cross-product netting, and termination-tail commissions. A bounded anti-circumvention clause should protect identified introductions for a stated period without claiming ownership of all operator customers. Require itemized statements, reasonable audit access, payment dates, currency, and a dispute window long enough to inspect cohort evidence. Define ownership of publisher code, original editorial work, event schemas, and licensed source material. Allocate liability by responsibility, negotiate a meaningful cap with express exceptions, and specify governing law, forum, escalation, and emergency relief. Do not accept unilateral fee changes that retroactively rewrite already qualified events or completed service periods.

Reconcile the canonical Formula v2.0 outcomes before inventing a growth narrative. Conservative revenue of $75,000 less $55,500 costs produces $19,500 owner profit and a 26% margin. Base revenue of $362,500 less $224,750 costs produces $137,750 and 38.0%. Scaled revenue of $650,000 less $325,000 costs produces $325,000 and 50%. Staffing remains 1 FT + 2 C, 1 FT + 2 C, and 2 FT + 3 C respectively. An illustrative allocation, not an additional scorecard assumption, assigns Conservative revenue to $45,000 subscriptions, $6,000 permitted builder fees, and $24,000 earned affiliate commissions. Base assigns $144,000, $18,500, and $200,000; Scaled assigns $240,000, $30,000, and $380,000. Each allocation sums exactly to its canonical total. Assess ASC 606 principal-versus-agent treatment for each contractual promise; the scorecard's gross-revenue label does not mean gross player deposits, sportsbook handle, or casino stakes. Affiliate revenue is the operator's earned commission after contractual revenue-share deductions, with applicable reversals and variable-consideration constraints. No numerical retained_share factor is supplied here, so do not fabricate one or multiply an already net commission by another retention percentage. Keep pass-through amounts outside recognized operator revenue when the accounting assessment requires net presentation.

A reproducible Base affiliate bridge uses 500 accepted FTDS at $300 each for $150,000 CPA revenue, with FTD defined in the contract as first-time depositor. A separate illustrative revenue-share cohort generates $300,000 contractual gross gaming revenue, less $50,000 bonuses, $30,000 administration charges, and $20,000 specified gaming taxes, leaving $200,000 NGR. A 30% share yields $60,000; a contractually defined $10,000 commission-account carryover reduces payable earned commissions to $50,000. Do not subtract that carryover from NGR instead unless the contract defines that different method. Total affiliate revenue is $200,000. Deduct $60,000 attributable CAC and $40,000 affiliate operating expense to produce $100,000 contribution, a 50% affiliate margin. The separate $162,500 software and builder lane bears $124,750 expense, producing $37,750; combined profit is the canonical $137,750. Expense allocations must reconcile once, without duplicating shared payroll. Stress the same model for post-NFL budget cuts: losing 100 accepted CPA events removes $30,000 revenue. With unchanged costs, profit falls to $107,750; that is a sensitivity, not a replacement Base case. If NGR deductions expand or carryover persists, suspend paid acquisition, negotiate cohort isolation, and favor subscriptions with measurable retention instead of buying more low-quality deposits.

callout.body: The best acquisition contract can be recalculated from its evidence. Negotiate the statement structure and test events before negotiating larger traffic commitments.

sections.heading: 4. Use permission-based scripts and evidence-led publication partnerships
paragraphs: Treat parasitic_seo, the Parasitic SEO & High-DR Subfolder Leasing play, as a contracted distribution experiment rather than a search-ranking entitlement. The play's DR 80-plus placement and rank-one-to-three within 48 hours targets are acquisition hypotheses, not delivery claims. DR is a third-party metric, not a Google authorization. Paid third-party pages placed mainly to exploit host reputation may violate search policies even when commercially documented. Partner with topically aligned trade publications that retain meaningful editorial review, publish original comparisons and calculators, and distinguish sponsored relationships. Require approved domains, publication standards, appropriate sponsored-link attributes, correction rights, takedown timing, attribution fields, and migration rights. An illustrative $1,200 monthly placement generating 2,000 visits at a 3% click-through rate produces 60 outbound visits; a 5% accepted-FTD rate produces three CPA events. At $300 each, revenue is $900, leaving a $300 loss before editorial and operating expense. Do not hide the loss behind ranking screenshots. If discovery underperforms or platform policy risk increases, end the lease and use aligned editorial partnerships as top-of-funnel feeders into owned email lists and separately authorized SMS lists. Preserve audience permission records; publication traffic does not itself create permission to message individual readers.

Use this operator outreach script verbatim after replacing only the factual identity and territory fields with verified details: 'Hello, I run a non-custodial research and comparison publisher. We are evaluating your licensed offering for audiences in our documented permitted territories. We do not accept player funds or place bets. Please send your affiliate service classification requirements, approved traffic sources, CPA acceptance definition, and itemized NGR schedule. We will activate links only after the required permissions and destination controls are documented. Who owns partner onboarding and monthly settlement?' Follow with this discovery script: 'Which legal entity signs, which products and territories are covered, and what credential must our entity hold? What makes an FTD payable? Which deductions apply before our share, how does negative carryover work, and can casino losses offset sportsbook commissions? Please show a sample statement and rejected-event report. Who can authorize changes, and how much notice applies?' These questions expose incompatible settlement terms before integration work. Record answers against the draft contract rather than relying on meeting memory. If the partner will not document deductions or classification responsibilities, stop commercial onboarding and continue only general, unlinked research until the missing terms are resolved in writing.

Use this publication script verbatim: 'We propose an original, clearly disclosed comparison guide for your existing gaming or market-structure audience. Your editors retain review and correction rights. We will identify compensated links, exclude prohibited destinations, and maintain jurisdiction-specific calls to action. We are buying defined editorial distribution, not promised search positions. Please confirm placement duration, permitted link treatment, access to aggregate performance reports, and removal or migration rights.' For customer discovery, use: 'Which probability comparisons do you currently rebuild manually, how frequently do stale quotes interrupt that work, and what would make a research subscription useful? Our service publishes analytics; it does not accept funds or execute transactions. Would you like one product summary by email?' Record that answer without treating it as SMS authorization. The first commercial email must identify the sender, include the required postal address, explain why the recipient is receiving it, and provide a functional opt-out. Use separate, clearly described authorization for promotional texts when required and synchronize revocations across vendors. Run the four-step launch procedure below before sending production traffic. Keep outreach truthful: do not claim registration is pending unless an application actually exists, and do not describe an operator relationship as active before the agreement takes effect.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #49, Regulated Prediction-Market Terminals & Licensed iGaming Affiliates, ranks #18 of 49 with a 91/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. This chapter maps 12 operator plays into a Python-led system for licensed feed normalization, probability analytics, subscription delivery, geofenced attribution, and evidence-led distribution. One full-time owner and two contractors can target 70% net repetitive-work reduction by automating deterministic handling while retaining human decisions over settlement equivalence, jurisdiction eligibility, advertising claims, and commission disputes. Canonical annual owner profits remain $19,500 Conservative, $137,750 Base, and $325,000 Scaled. The architecture separates non-custodial analytics and permitted builder revenue from licensed affiliate CPA and adjusted NGR commissions, measures automation costs per run, and stops distribution when evidence becomes stale.

sections.heading: 1. Build an evidence-carrying event backbone before adding AI
paragraphs: Assign the full-time owner commercial decisions, jurisdiction policy, and release authority; assign one contractor feed engineering and the other editorial evidence plus attribution reconciliation. Establish a time study before claiming automation. An illustrative week contains 1,000 minutes of repetitive research, qualification, fulfillment, and acquisition work. Deterministic jobs eliminate 760 minutes, but exception handling and sampling add 60 minutes, leaving 300 minutes and a 70% net reduction. This measures the repetitive-work denominator, not total labor or the disappearance of judgment. Instrument every task with baseline minutes, machine completion, correction minutes, and final disposition. Map twelve chapter-local plays across ingestion, analytics, subscription delivery, affiliate attribution, and distribution; the required external identifier is preserved in the second matrix. These descriptive mappings do not assert an additional proprietary play catalog. Give each production event an immutable identifier, source entitlement, jurisdiction context, acquisition timestamp, and transformation version. Use Python services, PostgreSQL, a durable queue such as Amazon SQS, and object storage with retention controls. A three-person team benefits more from replayable evidence than from a collection of autonomous agents. Test whether another team member can reconstruct a displayed probability or commission amount without asking its original author.

Build separate adapters for Kalshi, authorized ForecastEx access, and licensed sportsbook data. Verify current documentation, redistribution rights, rate limits, and account permissions before selecting transport. Do not assume ForecastEx or every sportsbook exposes a public WebSocket; use an authorized broker or distributor feed where required, and label polling latency honestly. For entitled streaming sources, set an illustrative sub-second internal objective of 150 milliseconds for receipt and decoding, 200 for normalization, 200 for comparison, and 150 for dashboard delivery, totaling 700 milliseconds. This excludes upstream publication delay and is a measured service objective rather than a venue promise. Python async workers validate payload schemas, attach sequence identifiers when available, and write an append-only event record before updating the latest-price cache. Use decimal arithmetic for prices and fees, explicit UTC timestamps, and synchronized clocks. A sequence gap triggers snapshot recovery; an expired entitlement disables the adapter instead of silently scraping around restrictions. Reject crossed books, impossible probabilities, and missing settlement definitions. During feed interruption, show the last verified timestamp and suppress actionable alerts. Never substitute a sportsbook moneyline for an event-contract price merely because both mention the same election, game, or economic release.

Create a versioned contract-equivalence registry before calculating cross-venue opportunity. Store settlement authority, observation window, overtime treatment, cancellation conditions, contract multiplier, fees, and available depth. A human approves each new equivalence pair; automation may reuse that decision only while those attributes remain unchanged. For a one-dollar binary payoff priced at $0.52, an estimated probability of 0.56 and an illustrative $0.01 execution charge produce $0.03 expected value per contract: 0.56 minus 0.52 minus 0.01. This estimate is sensitive to model error and does not establish executable arbitrage. Sportsbook odds of minus 110 imply 110 divided by 210, or 52.38%, before accounting for the opposing side and bookmaker margin. Normalize complete markets rather than treating that number as an independent fair probability. Keep the terminal non-custodial: no deposits, pooled positions, account credentials, or order submission. The Commodity Exchange Act definitions in 7 U.S.C. 1a distinguish introducing brokers, futures commission merchants, and commodity trading advisors; publisher positioning alone does not resolve registration. Have qualified counsel evaluate actual solicitation, compensation, personalization, and transaction involvement before activating builder referrals or individualized features. Reject unlicensed offshore, crypto-venue, and unlawful sweepstakes destinations from the eligible destination registry.

sections.heading: 2. Turn research into distribution without outsourcing truth
paragraphs: Use an LLM for bounded extraction, classification, and drafting, never as the authority for venue eligibility or statutory interpretation. A research worker retrieves permitted documents, records their content hashes, and supplies quoted passages to a schema-constrained request. Required fields include claim text, supporting passage, publication date, jurisdiction, and whether the claim changes customer eligibility. Treat retrieved pages as untrusted data: instructions embedded in a document cannot modify system permissions, request secrets, or authorize publication. Validate returned fields with Python, compare numerical assertions against deterministic calculations, and route missing evidence to an exception queue. An illustrative daily batch costs $12.00 for 10,000 deterministic jobs at $0.0012, $10.80 for 600 LLM extraction jobs at $0.018, and $3.00 for 400 webhook jobs at $0.0075. Total variable processing cost is $25.80 across 11,000 jobs, approximately $0.00235 per job. These are budgeting assumptions, not vendor quotations; data subscriptions, fixed hosting, human review, and acquisition spend remain separate. Fifteen review minutes at $40 per hour add $10.00, raising batch processing and sampled review to $35.80. Meter actual tokens, retries, cache hits, and reviewer time before using the estimate to price subscriptions.

Implement llm_citation_geo_poisoning, the TRACK_2 Generative Engine Optimization and AI-Overview Citation Seeding mapping, strictly as transparent citation research and factual publishing. The identifier does not authorize hidden instructions, fabricated endorsements, or manipulation of another system's retrieval behavior. Build a fixed panel of commercial buyer prompts covering terminal pricing, settlement comparisons, supported jurisdictions, and sportsbook affiliate economics. Inspect visible citations in ChatGPT Search, Perplexity, Gemini, and Google AI Overviews where those products actually return citations; record date, locale, prompt, cited domain, and quoted claim. Observations describe visible results, not private ranking logic or a reproducible default recommendation. Publish entity-dense comparison tables on the owned site and seek authorized editorial contributions on relevant cited trade domains. Budget twenty reviewed prompt observations at three minutes each, or one hour; at $40 per hour, research costs $40 before publication work. If an illustrative $160 total placement-and-research batch generates eight incremental trials, acquisition cost is $20 per trial, not per paying customer. Fall back to visible factual tables, accurate schema.org JSON-LD matching page content, and corroboration across independent trade publications when citations fluctuate. Disclose paid relationships and never invent an independent editorial endorsement.

Build the distribution flywheel around reusable evidence rather than unlimited page generation. A verified settlement comparison can feed a canonical reference page, an opt-in newsletter, a shareable chart, and a targeted partnership pitch. Every derivative retains the source timestamp and links back to the same versioned explanation. Programmatic pages require distinct operator facts, actual eligible products, and reviewed jurisdiction language; block empty state permutations and pages whose primary function is redirecting visitors. Public charts omit account identifiers, positions, and personalized recommendations. An illustrative cohort of 100 subscribers generates twenty voluntary chart shares; if those produce sixty qualified visits, twelve trials, and three paid accounts, the share loop contributes three accounts rather than a claimed viral multiplier. At $30 monthly SaaS revenue and $8 incremental delivery cost, each account contributes $22 before fixed costs. A $66 acquisition cost therefore requires three retained months for contribution payback. Keep gaming acquisition attribution separate from this SaaS cohort. Outbound messages target relevant business contacts, identify the sender, provide a working opt-out, and respect 15 U.S.C. 7704. Use human review for new claims, new partner categories, and materially changed offers; pause distribution when a cited price, license, or commercial term expires.

callout.body: The durable advantage is a maintained comparison record that partners, readers, and search products can independently verify.

sections.heading: 3. Reconcile affiliate cashflows without confusing them with SaaS
paragraphs: Treat affiliate measurement as a separate revenue subledger, not another terminal engagement metric. Before displaying a gaming offer, the policy service checks jurisdiction, destination license, applicable affiliate registration, campaign eligibility, and the platform's 21+ access policy. Ontario generally uses a different statutory age threshold for these products; a 21+ platform rule is a stricter product decision, not a claim about Ontario law. Use appropriately licensed geolocation evidence and operator confirmation rather than treating an IP address as conclusive location proof. Partner suitability differs among New Jersey DGE, Pennsylvania PGCB, Michigan MGCB, West Virginia Lottery, and Ontario AGCO or iGaming Ontario arrangements. Record the actual authorization needed for each relationship. A signed server-to-server callback carries a pseudonymous click identifier, operator conversion identifier, event type, currency, event time, and campaign version. Python verifies the signature over the original bytes, checks the replay window, and inserts an idempotency key scoped to operator and event. Browser pixels remain diagnostic rather than the commission ledger. The operator's qualifying FTD definition controls whether an event earns payment; a registration alone does not. Publish relevant responsible-gaming resources, exclude prohibited audiences and offers, and retain only attribution fields necessary for contracted measurement and dispute resolution.

Reconcile NGR using the signed agreement's actual order of operations. In the illustrative Base affiliate component, 600 accepted annual FTDs at $200 generate $120,000 CPA revenue. Separately, $250,000 of operator gaming revenue before contractual deductions, less $50,000 of permitted administration and bonus deductions, leaves a $200,000 sharing base. A 30% retained share produces $60,000, and $10,000 of commission-level negative carryover reduces recognized commission to $50,000, assuming those amounts are earned and collectible. Total affiliate revenue is therefore $170,000. Do not add the operator's $250,000 to this business's revenue, and do not treat player deposits as revenue. Some agreements apply carryover before sharing, segregate products, or reset balances; parameterize those differences rather than forcing this example onto every contract. If $60,000 acquisition spend, $30,000 allocated labor, and $15,000 infrastructure and operations support this component, affiliate contribution after those costs is $65,000, or 38.24% of $170,000. Separate CPA and RevShare cohorts unless the contract explicitly permits a hybrid payment. A reviewer matches operator statements to callbacks, reversal events, invoices, and cash receipts, while disputed deductions remain separately tracked rather than hidden inside a blended conversion-rate dashboard.

Preserve the canonical Formula v2.0 totals while labeling component allocations as illustrative. Conservative revenue consists here of $45,000 SaaS, zero builder rebates, and $30,000 net affiliate commissions, totaling $75,000. Expenses of $55,500 leave $19,500 owner net profit and a 26% margin with one full-time owner and two contractors. Base revenue comprises $180,000 SaaS, $12,500 permitted builder revenue, and $170,000 affiliate commissions, totaling $362,500. Expenses of $224,750 leave $137,750 and exactly 38.0%. Within that allocation, the non-affiliate component earns $192,500 against $119,750 expenses, leaving $72,750; add affiliate contribution of $65,000 to reconcile the total. Scaled revenue comprises $330,000 SaaS, $20,000 permitted builder revenue, and $300,000 affiliate commissions, totaling $650,000. Expenses of $325,000 leave $325,000 and 50% with two full-time people and three contractors. Apply ASC 606 principal-versus-agent analysis to the actual arrangement: a referral agent generally recognizes its earned commission, while its own SaaS subscription follows its service contract. Builder payments require separate eligibility and earning evidence. Budget sportsbook CPA seasonality explicitly: an illustrative 360 FTDs during six active months and 240 during six quieter months still total 600, without assuming football-season acquisition efficiency continues throughout the year.

sections.heading: 4. Operate the exception queue and scale only verified loops
paragraphs: Design recovery before increasing event volume. The ingestion worker writes a durable receipt before acknowledging delivery; downstream handlers make state changes through transactional outbox records and idempotent consumers. Duplicate callbacks should produce one ledger effect, not two commissions. Partition retries by cause: transient network failures receive bounded exponential backoff with jitter, authentication failures disable the affected connection, and schema changes enter a dead-letter queue for engineering review. A poison message cannot occupy the only worker indefinitely. Preserve the original payload under restricted access and attach a redacted diagnostic record to the incident. For market data, prioritize current state recovery over replaying every stale alert; the dashboard shows a freshness warning until the snapshot and incremental stream agree. For attribution, replay historical events because accounting completeness matters, but never overwrite an accepted event without a traceable correction. An illustrative incident objective is detection within two minutes and initial classification within fifteen minutes during staffed coverage. Outside coverage, automatically suppress affected alerts or offers rather than implying continuous human supervision. Test restoration from backups and replay a known callback batch every month. A backup that has never reconstructed a ledger is merely an untested storage expense.

Set review intensity according to consequence and novelty. Humans inspect every new jurisdiction rule, venue-equivalence pair, personalized feature, promotional claim, and material contract change before release. Stable extraction jobs receive stratified samples that include each source, model version, and jurisdiction; exceptions receive complete review. As an illustrative policy, inspect thirty of 600 routine extraction outputs daily, plus all outputs with missing sources or changed eligibility language. At thirty seconds per routine sample, the sample consumes fifteen minutes, but complex statutory review requires additional separately budgeted time. Sampling does not validate the uninspected population individually. Track defect classes, severity, correction minutes, and how many customers received an incorrect result. Any consequential eligibility or payment defect pauses the affected automation class until the root cause is fixed and replay tests pass. Use a versioned evaluation set containing settlement cancellations, ambiguous timestamps, duplicate FTD callbacks, carryover reversals, and misleading source instructions. Compare candidate model releases against the current version on these cases before switching. Keep a deterministic extraction fallback for essential fields and a manual queue for unstructured material. The owner signs off on consequential decisions rather than treating a confidence score as delegated authority.

Scale the narrow loops that produce retained contribution, not the loops with the largest impression counts. A weekly operating sheet joins subscription cohorts, source-level acquisition costs, affiliate statement adjustments, automation expense, and correction labor without mixing customer trading volume into revenue. Compare paid, programmatic, referral, and citation-led channels using the same attribution window and explicitly record assisted touches rather than counting one customer several times. For the $30 subscription with $8 incremental monthly delivery cost, a six-month retained customer contributes $132 before acquisition and fixed expenses. Spending $66 leaves $66 over those six months; a customer leaving after two months contributes only $44 and does not recover that acquisition cost. Gaming CPA offers need their own accepted-event and reversal assumptions, especially after NFL budgets contract. Promote one change at a time through shadow calculation, limited exposure, and measured expansion, with a recorded rollback owner. Move from the Base three-person configuration to the Scaled five-person configuration only when contracted revenue, queue age, and review workload support the additional capacity. Automation succeeds when each additional customer requires less repetitive handling while evidence quality remains intact. The flywheel is verified data becoming useful distribution, then retained revenue funding better data and faster corrections.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #49, Rank #18 of 49, scores 91/100 by combining non-custodial prediction-market software with separately controlled licensed affiliate media. This chapter assigns 12 mapped plays to a three-person pod, then expands only when a five-person structure improves verified contribution and continuity. The canonical annual owner-profit cases are $19,500 Conservative, $137,750 Base, and $325,000 Scaled. Contractor scorecards connect delivery acceptance to data integrity, earned commissions, and transferable intellectual property rather than traffic vanity. Separate ledgers expose NGR deductions, negative carryover, and football-season acquisition risk. Concentration limits, written assignments, reproducible accruals, and replacement-cost normalization support either an evidence-based sale discussion or a durable owner-operated cash business.

sections.heading: 1. Allocate twelve plays without creating twelve jobs
paragraphs: Build the initial pod around one full-time owner and two bounded contractor seats, not a collection of founders sharing every decision. The owner controls product priorities, cash, counterparty contracting, jurisdiction eligibility, and weekly acceptance. Contractor A owns ingestion, normalization, alert delivery, and instrumentation. Contractor B owns licensed affiliate publishing, attribution reconciliation, support triage, and evidence assembly. For this chapter, map the candidate's twelve plays into explicit operating workstreams: P01 event-contract terminal; P02 cross-venue probability comparison; P03 positive-expectation alerts; P04 subscription packaging; P05 permitted builder referrals; P06 sportsbook comparison; P07 casino comparison; P08 jurisdiction-specific acquisition; P09 first-time-depositor attribution; P10 CPA settlement recovery; P11 NGR cohort optimization; and P12 retention and renewal. These are an execution mapping, not twelve independent revenue forecasts. Put each deliverable in Linear or GitHub Issues with one accountable seat, acceptance evidence, and a rollback owner. A publishing task cannot quietly authorize account opening, order solicitation, trade execution, or custody. Keep application permissions aligned with that distinction: read-only market access where available, no withdrawal credentials, and no customer trading secrets. The owner must identify the actual venue, intermediary, data license, and permitted commercial relationship before any play becomes a live product feature.

Translate responsibility into purchased capacity. An illustrative Base contract buys sixty engineering hours monthly at $50 per hour and forty revenue-operations hours at $50, producing $36,000 and $24,000 annual contractor budgets. These amounts sit inside the canonical expense envelope; they are not incremental charges layered onto its profit. Conservative capacity must shrink substantially, because $75,000 revenue supports only $55,500 total annual expenses. Buy fixed acceptance bundles, limit active campaigns, and avoid promising continuous human coverage. Engineering invoices require a reproducible test, deployment record, and documented recovery procedure. Revenue-operations invoices require reviewed publisher pages, matched commission records, and dated jurisdiction evidence. Specify severity-one acknowledgement within two contracted coverage hours and immediate automated suppression of stale signals outside those hours. Routine defects receive a two-business-day triage target; accepted deliverables include one correction cycle within the contracted scope. Tie any bonus to collected, validated contribution after reversals, never raw deposits or user losses. Use written change orders for additional work, pay undisputed accepted work on schedule, and assess worker classification under applicable federal and state tests. A contract label alone does not determine employment status or justify imposing employee-like control.

Expand to two full-time seats and three contractors only after recurring contribution funds the second employee through a weak sportsbook quarter. The original owner becomes commercial general manager; the second employee becomes systems and operating-control lead. Retain engineering and editorial contractors, then add a settlement-and-cohort contractor as the third external seat. Split the former revenue-operations backlog rather than duplicating it. Assign P01 through P05 technically to the systems lead, P06 through P08 commercially to the owner, and P09 through P12 jointly through distinct production and acceptance duties. The producer never clears their own commission exception. At three people, the owner performs that second review; at five, the systems lead reviews reconciliation evidence while the owner authorizes payments. Episodic legal and tax advice remains separately budgeted professional-service spend, not a disguised permanent sixth operating seat. Document every recurring task sufficiently for another pod member to perform it during a two-week absence. Keep company-controlled repositories, domain registrations, billing accounts, and password-manager recovery accessible to two authorized people. Do not confuse redundancy with shared passwords. Test an actual restore and a sample settlement handoff before increasing subscriber commitments or adding another state-facing campaign to the workload.

callout.title: Purchase evidence, not a pile of contractor activity
callout.body: Small pods outperform larger publishing teams when contract acceptance creates reusable operating evidence rather than merely completed tasks.
items: Require engineering to replay a disconnected feed and prove that stale probability alerts stop before the next subscriber notification.
Keep a permitted-access register for Kalshi, ForecastEx, intermediaries, and sportsbook data vendors; a visible quote does not establish redistribution rights.
Pay settlement bonuses only on recovered, collected commission contribution after deductions, with later reversals handled under a written compensation schedule.
Have the alternate operator close one real weekly cohort during the owner's absence; a walkthrough alone does not establish transferability.

sections.heading: 2. Run a weekly scorecard that detects economic and jurisdiction failures
paragraphs: Run the weekly scorecard from a frozen Monday extract, not screenshots selected by each contractor. The engineering seat supplies feed availability, event-to-alert latency, stale suppression, incident duration, and unresolved severity counts. Measure latency from the timestamp actually available at the licensed source, distinguish upstream delay from internal processing, and publish the measurement population. A sub-second design ambition is not evidence that every market or vendor supports that service level. The revenue seat supplies paid subscription retention, refunds, validated FTDs, rejected FTD reasons, earned CPA, NGR deductions, carryover, collected cash, and cohort contribution. The owner supplies concentration, runway, registration status, and open contractual exceptions. Calculate contribution after attributable acquisition and delivery costs; separately show shared overhead so nobody mistakes campaign contribution for owner profit. Use Stripe exports for subscription evidence, Postgres for immutable event identifiers, and partner statements as settlement evidence. Store source file hashes and extraction timestamps beside each calculation. Every red metric needs a named corrective action, due date, and measurable recovery criterion. Do not reward a contractor for fixing attribution by rewriting history without a preserved correction record and an independent reviewer.

Set a concentration policy of no more than 25% for any single customer or counterparty, measured across both trailing-twelve-month recognized revenue and contribution. Aggregate related brands under their controlling group, because five sportsbook logos can represent one economic payer. Show contracted forward exposure and unpaid receivables alongside historical shares; a diversified historical chart can conceal next quarter's dependence. Where total contribution is zero or negative, suspend that percentage test and review absolute counterparty exposure instead of displaying a misleading ratio. During launch, a first customer necessarily breaches the revenue cap; label the business concentrated, restrict incremental acquisition against that payer, and establish a dated diversification plan. Do not advertise buyer-ready diversification until the actual books meet the policy. SaaS customers and affiliate payers belong in the combined economic concentration view, while each channel also retains its own analysis. Track feed-vendor and search-platform dependencies separately because revenue diversification does not eliminate infrastructure dependence. If the leading partner cuts CPA budgets after football season, pause marginal paid campaigns first, protect retained subscriptions, and model the next thirteen weeks of collections using signed terms rather than last season's peak conversion and promotional rates.

Make jurisdiction and activity boundaries measurable operating checks. The Commodity Exchange Act definitions of introducing broker and futures commission merchant turn on actual conduct, including solicitation, order acceptance, and receipt of customer assets; a non-custodial label is not a universal exemption. Assess paid advice and personalized analytics separately under the commodity trading adviser framework, including any applicable exclusion or exemption and its conditions. Refer uncertain feature changes for qualified review before release, while continuing clearly permitted publishing work. Never hold user funds, pool capital, or direct US customers to unlicensed offshore, crypto, or unlawful sweepstakes venues. For licensed affiliate pages, verify the operator's authorization and the publisher's own required status with NJ DGE, PA PGCB, MI MGCB, or the relevant jurisdiction. Treat Ontario as a separate Canadian operating regime, not another US state authorization. Apply the specified 21+ audience policy, jurisdiction-aware landing pages, responsible-gaming helpline disclosures, and clear compensation disclosures. Publisher geofencing does not replace the licensed operator's age, identity, or location checks. Store dated evidence for each active campaign and suppress destinations when permissions expire, an operator exits a market, or a landing-page change invalidates the previously accepted control record.

sections.heading: 3. Close separate books that reconcile exactly to the canonical cases
paragraphs: Preserve the Formula v2.0 totals before designing departmental budgets. Conservative revenue of $75,000 less $55,500 expenses produces $19,500 owner profit at 26%; Base revenue of $362,500 less $224,750 produces $137,750 at 38.0%; Scaled revenue of $650,000 less $325,000 produces $325,000 at 50%. The first two cases retain one full-time seat and two contractors; Scaled uses two full-time seats and three contractors. These are annual scorecard cases, not monthly run rates or promises about every cohort. Separate subscription revenue, permitted builder revenue, CPA commissions, and NGR commissions in the chart of accounts. A subscriber's event-contract turnover and a sportsbook customer's deposits never enter operator revenue. Neither does a merchant's entire gaming handle. The canonical gross-revenue label describes this operator's revenue basis; affiliate amounts already reflect contractual deductions rather than underlying gaming volume. Apply the principal-versus-agent analysis to actual contracts and document the ASC 606 conclusion. Do not multiply these canonical figures by an invented retained-share factor or subtract the same partner deductions again. Maintain reconciliation schedules from contractual gross commission calculations to the operator amounts actually recognized, then from recognized revenue to cash collected.

An illustrative Base bridge allocates $210,000 to subscriptions, $12,500 to permitted builder revenue, and $140,000 to net affiliate commissions, summing exactly to $362,500. Suppose affiliate statements begin with $180,000 of contract-calculated commissions before $40,000 of applicable administration, bonus, reversal, and carryover adjustments. The resulting $140,000 is the affiliate revenue line, not $180,000 plus an expense that later gets deducted twice. Allocate $85,000 of operating costs to affiliates, including $45,000 CAC and $40,000 delivery and allocated overhead, leaving $55,000 affiliate profit. The software and builder book carries $139,750 operating costs against $222,500 revenue, leaving $82,750. Together, costs equal $224,750 and profit equals $137,750. This allocation illustrates control design; it is not an additional canonical forecast. Retain the monthly source statement behind every deduction, including whether negative carryover crosses products, markets, or calendar periods. Model CPA seasonality at the contract and cohort level, not as a uniform haircut to recurring software subscriptions. Show a sensitivity where affiliate collections slow and acquisition rates fall, but keep that downside separate from the three fixed scorecard scenarios. Never silently replace the Base profit with a new sensitivity result.

Close monthly using service periods and earned rights, not bank deposits alone. Defer prepaid subscription amounts until the corresponding service is delivered, reconcile processor fees separately, and retain refund and chargeback schedules. Recognize CPA only when contractual qualification and the applicable variable-consideration assessment support the amount; a click or unvalidated first deposit is not automatically earned revenue. Accrue supportable builder rebates against their actual eligibility terms. Maintain an NGR rollforward by partner, jurisdiction, cohort, and settlement month, including opening carryover, current activity, deductions, offsets, and closing balance. Distinguish an unrecognized future hurdle from an existing payable obligation; the contract determines whether a negative balance can demand cash or only reduce later commissions. Post contractor costs when services are received and maintain an unbilled-services accrual at month end. Reconcile receivable aging to partner confirmations and subsequent collections, then review collectability. The owner signs the close after checking a sample from invoice through source evidence to bank receipt. Preserve locked monthly snapshots and journal explanations in the company data room. A buyer should reproduce twelve months of contribution without asking the founder to interpret an undocumented spreadsheet or retrieve messages from a personal account.

sections.heading: 4. Build a transferable asset and price the earnings actually being sold
paragraphs: Build the sale file while operating, because transferability cannot be manufactured during a buyer's final diligence week. Obtain signed present-tense assignments of relevant copyright from each actual rights owner under 17 U.S.C. section 204(a). Contractor software is not automatically owned by the customer merely because an invoice was paid, and commissioned work does not universally qualify as work made for hire. Identify pre-existing libraries, open-source components, licenses, model inputs, and third-party data separately from newly assigned work. Maintain a dependency inventory and evidence that the business can lawfully continue using each component after a transaction. Put repositories, domains, analytics properties, content archives, billing administration, and deployment recovery under company control. Inventory affiliate agreement assignment provisions, change-of-control rights, termination terms, post-termination commission tails, and personal guarantees. A buyer does not automatically inherit a gaming registration, a market-data entitlement, or a venue's builder arrangement. Obtain counterparty and regulator determinations required for the contemplated structure before assuming continuity. Prepare cohort-level diligence extracts with pseudonymous identifiers and controlled access; do not publish player-level records into an unrestricted data room. Transfer only data and permissions the transaction documents and applicable obligations actually support.

Use valuation ranges as explicit negotiation assumptions, not observed market quotations. For a small owner-operated asset, test 2.0 to 3.0 times normalized seller's discretionary earnings; for a genuinely manager-run, recurring, transferable operation, test 3.0 to 5.0 times adjusted EBITDA. These bases are different and cannot share the same unexplained profit number. Canonical owner profit is not automatically either measure. If diligence establishes Base owner profit of $137,750 as normalized SDE without further adjustments, the first range implies $275,500 to $413,250 enterprise value. That conditional calculation assumes the buyer will perform the owner's job. For a separate Scaled illustration, suppose $325,000 owner profit excludes a necessary $120,000 fully loaded replacement manager cost and contains no other normalization differences. Adjusted EBITDA would then be $205,000, and the second range implies $615,000 to $1,025,000 enterprise value. If replacement management is already expensed, subtracting it again would understate earnings. Confirm treatment from payroll and the actual ledger. Bridge enterprise value to equity proceeds through debt, cash treatment, working-capital terms, transaction costs, and contingent consideration. An earnout headline is not cash received at closing, and an unassignable major affiliate agreement can materially reduce both price and buyer willingness.

Earn a stronger multiple by removing specific buyer risks rather than adding presentation polish. Show twelve monthly closes with cohort continuity, independent acceptance, and actual collections. Demonstrate that no related customer or counterparty exceeds the 25% concentration caps, that acquired traffic remains profitable after football season, and that recurring subscribers renew without founder-led intervention. Produce a successful restore, a contractor replacement exercise, and a two-week owner absence with service and settlement metrics intact. Explain each of the twelve plays through a runbook link, permission record, revenue account, and responsible seat. Retire plays that generate complexity without durable contribution; a buyer can value four reliable engines more highly than twelve unproven pages. If sale terms depend on aggressive add-backs, personal relationships, or large contingent payments, retain the business and distribute only cash remaining after working capital, tax reserves, and required maintenance. Compare an actual cash offer with a conservative operating cash-flow plan, not a multiple applied to hypothetical peak-season earnings. Revisit the choice quarterly using the same accounting policies. Durable cash ownership and a credible exit share the same foundation: documented rights, separable books, replaceable labor, and revenue that survives an ordinary disruption.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #49, Regulated Prediction-Market Terminals & Licensed iGaming Affiliates, holds Rank #18 of 49 with a 91/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. This sprint turns 12 mapped plays into a controlled release operated by one full-time founder and two contractors. Separate subscription analytics, permitted builder payments, and licensed affiliate commissions before writing acquisition copy. Days 1–7 establish permissions and cash limits; Days 8–14 prove feed integrity and attribution; Days 15–21 test paid demand; Days 22–30 reconcile evidence and allocate the next dollar. Annual owner-profit cases remain $19,500 Conservative, $137,750 Base, and $325,000 Scaled. Day 30/60/90 decisions require measured retention, collected contribution, and jurisdiction-specific eligibility, rather than trading volume or optimistic commission dashboards. The first month builds evidence; first deals can still take two to six months.

sections.heading: 1. Days 1–7: Fix the Operating Boundary, Twelve-Play Map, and Cash Envelope
paragraphs: Day 1 starts with a boundary memorandum, not a trading interface. The founder owns product, publisher relationships, and cash; contractor C1 owns data engineering and reliability; contractor C2 owns editorial operations, attribution reconciliation, and coordination with qualified regulatory counsel. The pod remains one full-time person plus two contractors, with specialist consultations purchased as bounded services rather than hidden permanent headcount. Separate the analytics product from affiliate landing pages, contracts, event schemas, and ledgers. A user must never fund an operator wallet, delegate trading credentials, pool capital, or submit an order through this launch. Non-custody alone does not settle registration: solicitation, compensation, advice, and order-related activity also matter under 7 U.S.C. § 1a, 7 U.S.C. § 6d, and 17 CFR § 1.3. Obtain a written assessment of the actual functions and compensation before enabling them. A builder program agreement does not override federal registration requirements. Record excluded features explicitly, including personalized trade recommendations and execution links carrying order instructions. Public analytics must remain within the assessed scope; calling software a publisher does not create an exemption. Any unresolved classification stays disabled while ordinary engineering continues.

Use a local execution map for all twelve plays, so the chapter does not imply twelve simultaneous product launches. P01 is the non-custodial research terminal; P02 is authorized event-feed ingestion; P03 is contract and settlement normalization; P04 is cross-venue probability comparison; P05 is fee-adjusted positive-EV alerting; P06 is paid analytics subscriptions. P07 is permitted builder-payment software; P08 is jurisdiction-specific licensed-operator comparison publishing; P09 is sportsbook CPA acquisition; P10 is iGaming NGR participation; P11 is geofenced server-to-server attribution; P12 is retention and cohort reporting. These identifiers are this sprint's operational mapping, not an assertion that every partner offers every commercial rail. Activate P01–P06 first where authorized; treat P07–P11 as contract-dependent modules and use P12 across both businesses. The founder owns P06–P10, C1 owns P02–P05 and P11, and C2 owns P01 publishing and P12 reporting. Every handoff needs a named reviewer and a retained test artifact. Prioritize one event category, one subscription offer, and one permitted affiliate jurisdiction. NJ, PA, MI, WV, and ON are separate operating territories, not interchangeable license extensions. Ontario also has distinct advertising restrictions; a uniform 21+ product policy does not describe Ontario's statutory minimum.

Set the first thirty days' maximum cash outflow at the lesser of $10,000 or unrestricted startup cash minus a $3,000 untouched reserve. With $8,000 available, the cap is $5,000 and the sprint remains research and prototype work unless permissions and vendor costs fit; with $45,000 available, the cap still remains $10,000. Under the full envelope, allocate $2,400 to week one, $2,200 to week two, $2,200 to week three, and $3,200 to the final nine days. Within that envelope, earmark $3,000 for scoped regulatory and contract work, $3,000 for contractor delivery, $1,200 for feed, hosting, and software costs, $1,200 for permitted demand tests, and $1,600 for contingency. These are spending limits, not vendor quotes. Include prepaid services, filing payments, taxes on purchases, and founder cash draws when checking the ceiling; separately record unpaid founder hours. Cut acquisition and optional interfaces before consuming the reserve. The stated $1,500–$10,000 monthly operating range is an early operating envelope, not a ceiling on mature all-in scenario expenses. First-deal timing remains two to six months, so Day 30 can produce a verified prototype and partner pipeline without producing an authorized affiliate commission.

sections.heading: 2. Days 8–14: Prove Data Integrity, Eligible Referrals, and Separate Revenue Ledgers
paragraphs: Build the feed service around permissioned access, replayability, and economic comparability. Kalshi access and ForecastEx access through an authorized broker or data arrangement must be assessed separately; do not assume identical WebSocket availability, redistribution rights, or builder terms. Use an available licensed streaming interface where supported and approved polling otherwise. C1 stores source timestamps, receipt timestamps, market identifiers, settlement sources, fee versions, and sequence information when supplied. A sub-second internal target means p95 receipt-to-screen latency below 1,000 milliseconds across 10,000 measured updates, not a promise that upstream quotes are always current. Flag missing heartbeats and suppress alerts when quote age exceeds two seconds during active trading, with product-specific exceptions documented for slower sources. Compare contracts only when event definitions, settlement timing, cancellation rules, and payout units align. A binary quote of $0.54 is not directly comparable with sportsbook decimal odds without accounting for payout structure, fees, and differing outcomes. Store the transformation alongside the displayed number. Positive-EV labels require an explicit probability estimate, timestamp, and fee assumption; they are model outputs, not executable returns. Test suspended markets, corrections, reconnects, and settlement changes before allowing any automated alert to reach subscribers.

For affiliate attribution, define an eligible first-time depositor using the signed operator contract, not a universal marketing definition. Required conditions may include a new verified account, territory eligibility, qualifying deposit, minimum activity, attribution window, and exclusion of duplicate or prohibited users. C1 creates an opaque click identifier; C2 maintains the partner-specific conversion dictionary. Send no trading credentials or unnecessary identity documents through the affiliate system. Where supported, authenticate callbacks with signatures, enforce replay protection, and make conversion processing idempotent. A duplicate callback must not become a second CPA. Enforce jurisdiction restrictions before the outbound link, but recognize that IP location is a preliminary control and does not replace the operator's required geolocation and identity checks. Display material affiliate relationships clearly under 16 CFR § 255.5, near recommendations and comparison links. Apply the 21+ product policy and relevant responsible-gaming resources consistently; do not publish prohibited inducements or target excluded people. Reconcile click, accepted conversion, reversal, and paid settlement identifiers separately. An operator dashboard can report a pending depositor without creating an earned receivable. Where a partner supplies no test callback, use a clearly isolated synthetic fixture and require subsequent production reconciliation before increasing acquisition.

The accounting design must prevent throughput from masquerading as operator revenue. Subscription revenue follows delivered service and applicable refund treatment; annual prepayments are not automatically first-month earned revenue. Builder payments enter their own ledger only when the program actually exists, the operator is eligible, and the contractual earning conditions are satisfied. Affiliate economics use the commission entitlement after contractual deductions, not deposited funds, betting handle, or customer winnings. For an illustrative NGR contract, $30,000 of operator-defined gaming revenue less $6,000 of allowable bonus and administration deductions produces $24,000 eligible NGR. A 25% commission creates $6,000 before any affiliate-level carryover; a documented $1,000 carryover offset leaves $5,000 before acquisition and servicing expenses. Whether deductions apply before or after the percentage depends on the signed schedule. Preserve that ordering in executable tests. Under an ASC 606 principal-versus-agent assessment, any retained_share bridge uses the operator's actual retained consideration, not customer stakes as gross billings. Do not deduct the same bonus twice through both revenue and expense. Maintain accrued revenue, cash received, deferred service obligations, and disputed commissions as distinct fields. Day 14 ends only after the founder can reproduce each dollar from contract to event to ledger.

callout.title: Four Tactics That Protect a Small Pod from Expensive False Positives
callout.body: Most apparent early wins disappear through incompatible contract terms, duplicated conversions, or settlement deductions. Preserve evidence before buying traffic.
items: Version market-resolution language alongside price snapshots; a cheap-looking contract with a different cancellation rule is not a comparable opportunity.
Request anonymized historical settlement examples before accepting NGR terms, including one negative month and the following month's carryover treatment.
Capture the sportsbook's current CPA budget window and model a 50% off-season payout reduction with unchanged CAC before committing acquisition spend.
Export partner settlement files before dashboard retention expires, then reconcile reversals to the original click and cohort rather than the current reporting month.

sections.heading: 3. Days 15–21: Test Paid Demand Without Corrupting the Canonical Economics
paragraphs: Days 15–21 test whether eligible users will pay for a narrow analytical job, not whether advertising can generate impressive account counts. Interview twenty prospects who match the chosen use case and record their existing tools, decision frequency, and willingness to purchase without promised winnings. Define an activated trial as a person who completes onboarding, views a correctly normalized comparison, and returns on a second day. Use a single illustrative $49 monthly subscription during the experiment; this test price does not reconstruct the annual scorecard's customer mix. Five paying accounts would produce $245 of monthly recurring subscription value before refunds, rather than evidence of the Base annual case. Track CAC separately for subscription buyers and accepted affiliate depositors. Allocate shared creative and contractor work by recorded hours or another documented driver. Affiliate contribution equals earned net commissions less acquisition, variable servicing, and allocated operating costs. If acquisition is paused for permissions, do not manufacture demand using employee deposits or incentivized accounts that breach partner terms. Continue interviews, interface tests, and partner negotiations instead. C2 reviews every comparison claim, while the founder approves spending in daily increments against the remaining week-three envelope. C1 fixes reliability before adding features.

Reconcile the annual cases before interpreting any launch conversion. The canonical Conservative case is $75,000 revenue less $55,500 total modeled expenses, yielding $19,500 owner profit and a 26% margin. Base is $362,500 less $224,750, yielding $137,750 and 38.0%. Scaled is $650,000 less $325,000, yielding $325,000 and 50%. An illustrative stream allocation that preserves those totals is Conservative $50,000 subscriptions, $5,000 permitted builder payments, and $20,000 net affiliate commissions; Base $240,000, $12,500, and $110,000 respectively; Scaled $420,000, $30,000, and $200,000 respectively. Those allocations are planning bridges, not additional canonical assumptions. Every affiliate figure is already net of contractual revenue deductions. Each scenario excludes trading volume, merchant handle, deposits, loan principal, and customer assets. Conservative and Base use one full-time operator plus two contractors; Scaled uses two full-time operators plus three contractors. The five-person case cannot be claimed while silently outsourcing equivalent work outside its expenses. Annual expenses exceed early monthly fixed overhead where acquisition, delivery, and other modeled costs expand. Neither a successful launch week nor an annualized subscription snapshot establishes these profit outcomes. Review the expense bridge by stream before deciding which marginal acquisition dollar deserves funding.

For a Base-compatible affiliate worksheet, start with $160,000 in annual commission accruals before contractual adjustments. Subtract $25,000 of documented administration and bonus adjustments, $10,000 of applicable carryover offsets, and $15,000 of reversals to reach $110,000 recognized affiliate revenue. Deduct $36,000 acquisition cost and $18,000 allocated delivery and overhead to produce $56,000 affiliate profit, or 50.91% of recognized affiliate revenue. This worksheet assumes those adjustments are commission-level amounts; an NGR-level contract requires recalculation before applying the revenue-share percentage. The remaining $252,500 of subscription and builder revenue carries $170,750 of expenses and $81,750 profit, so combined profit remains exactly $137,750. For seasonality, stress-test an isolated CPA cohort with forty accepted depositors: $200 per depositor yields $8,000 earned commission, while $120 CAC and $800 servicing leave $2,400 contribution. At a $100 off-season CPA, unchanged spending produces a $1,600 loss. That sensitivity is not a replacement scorecard scenario. Pause that cohort rather than averaging its loss into profitable subscriptions. Maintain NGR carryover separately by the contractual pooling unit, and record settlement delays in runway calculations. A positive accrued margin with cash arriving after payroll can still exhaust the sprint reserve.

sections.heading: 4. Days 22–30 and Reviews at 60/90: Allocate Cash Through Explicit Kill, Fix, or Scale Decisions
paragraphs: The final nine days turn measurements into an operating decision. Day 22 freezes the cohort dictionary; Day 23 exercises stale-feed and duplicate-callback failures; Day 24 reconciles collections; Day 25 retests territory restrictions; Day 26 reviews retention; Day 27 closes contract issues; Day 28 reruns seasonal sensitivity; Day 29 prepares the evidence packet; Day 30 assigns each rail a disposition. A critical incident means custody or order-taking outside scope, a prohibited territory referral, exposed credentials, or unauthorized data distribution. Any single such incident stops the affected function immediately; repair and re-verification precede resumption. For analytics, paid retention means eligible starting subscribers still paying after thirty days, excluding newly added accounts from the numerator. CAC payback equals acquisition cost per new paying subscriber divided by monthly subscriber contribution before acquisition cost. Use observed contribution after refunds, payment fees, variable data, and support. For affiliates, contribution margin uses recognized net commissions as its denominator and includes acquisition plus allocated servicing in its costs. Do not combine CPA depositor counts with subscription accounts. A small sample receives a Fix disposition with a bounded measurement task, not a fabricated confidence claim. Evaluate cash runway using unrestricted funds and committed outflows, not unpaid commissions.

Day 30 Scale means permission to expand a verified experiment, not permission to adopt the Scaled annual forecast. Require zero open critical incidents, all blocking-route tests passing, at least twenty qualified interviews, ten activated trials, and five paying analytics subscribers where sales are permitted. Increase the next thirty-day discretionary experiment budget by at most 25%, only when a thirteen-week cash forecast preserves the reserve. Without completed commercial permissions, keep acquisition at zero and assess the partner pipeline instead. Require at least two documented partner discussions and one written list of remaining requirements with an accountable counterparty. A slow decision within the stated two-to-six-month deal window is not itself a failed business. Day 60 requires thirty paying subscribers and at least twenty renewal-eligible accounts showing 80% thirty-day paid retention before subscription acquisition expands. Affiliate expansion needs thirty settled accepted depositors, at least 20% cohort contribution margin, and settlement reconciliation within 1% by value. An unresolved larger difference pauses spending until explained. Subscription and affiliate rails can receive different decisions on the same day. Never use subscription cash to hide an affiliate cohort that fails its own contribution test.

At Day 90, require sixty paying subscribers, at least forty renewal-eligible accounts, 85% thirty-day paid retention, and CAC payback no longer than six months before scaling subscription acquisition again. Affiliate expansion needs sixty settled accepted depositors spanning two complete cohorts, each contributing at least 20% after acquisition and allocated servicing, with nonnegative contribution under the 50% CPA reduction stress. NGR-heavy rails need two complete settlement cycles and explicit carryover reconciliation instead of borrowing a CPA depositor test. These are management thresholds, not scorecard inputs or industry benchmarks. Kill means retire a channel or feature whose evidence meets the failure condition; it does not automatically close a profitable independent rail. Fix means a named owner, a fourteen-day deadline, and spending restricted to remediation and existing service. Scale means at most another 25% discretionary budget increase while the same pod can meet support and reconciliation service levels. Require 95% of support requests answered within one business day and weekly closes completed within two business days. If either fails for two weeks, stop expansion and repair workload first. Move to two full-time staff plus three contractors only through an explicit capacity and expense plan, never by treating automation as evidence that review work disappeared.
